Most supporters were still walking into the ground when the former struck first ball, Azan Awais lbw to a nip-backer. Shan Masood’s stilted footwork was ripe for exposing and Robinson’s first ball over the wicket to the left-hander was full and straight to beat the loose drive.

Imam-ul-Haq had done the hard work, seeing off Robinson only to flash a drive to second slip off a wide ball from Tongue to end Pakistan’s only stand of substance of the innings: 93 for the third wicket.

Robinson cracked the innings open further with Saud Shakeel leg before, who was too slow to call for the review that would have saved him. Hawk-Eye showed the ball would have gone over the top.

Robinson then bowled Shafique in his next over and Pakistan were toppling. Tongue cranked up the pace, bowled full and the perpendicular angle into the right-handers did the rest.

News.title: Burnham blames Trump’s war in Iran for higher inflation
News.content:
Andy Burnham has blamed Donald Trump’s war in Iran for higher inflation in Britain.

Inflation jumped from 2.6pc in June to 2.9pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics, threatening to undermine Mr Burnham’s pledge to bring down the cost of living.

The Prime Minister said: “We can’t control though what is going on in the Middle East and the effect of the conflict there is now being felt in inflation here, and in other countries around the world.

“I realise these times are really hard but already people can see a month into office I have done things that will make a difference.”

July’s inflation figure was affected by a 13.5pc rise in the Ofgem price cap in response to the energy crisis unleashed by the Iran war. It means prices are now rising at their highest rate since March.

The latest figure shows the struggle that Mr Burnham faces to fulfil his promise to bring down living costs.

There are fears that inflation will climb higher in the coming months as the impact of the conflict filters through to the economy.

Speaking at an event in the North East, Mr Burnham added: “I want to lead a cost-of-living Government, and I’ve already taken steps as Prime Minister to show I will help people wherever I can. I can’t do everything, I think people know that.

“We’re in tough times, but where I can do something to make life that little bit better, I will do it.”

Since arriving in No 10, Mr Burnham has made tackling the cost of living a key policy focus.

The Prime Minister announced last month that he would remove VAT from electricity bills from October and reinstate the £2 cap on bus fares from next year.

However, average energy bills are expected to jump by around 4pc from October, according to energy analysts Cornwall Insight, wiping out any potential savings from Mr Burnham’s VAT cut.

The analysts said Ofgem’s price cap – which limits the average annual energy bill faced by a family home – would rise from £1,663 to £1,729.

Despite concerns about increasing gas and electricity bills, July’s rate of inflation was in line with economists’ expectations.

Money markets now expect policymakers at the Bank of England to hold interest rates at 3.75pc at their next meeting in September.

News.title: Unemployment rate fails to fall for Burnham
News.content:
An expected drop in the unemployment rate has failed to materialise, dealing a setback to Andy Burnham’s hopes of reviving Britain’s ailing economy.

Unemployment remained stuck at 4.9pc in the three months to June, while the number of payrolled employees fell by 13,000, according to figures from the Office for National Statistics. Economists had predicted that the unemployment rate would ease to 4.8pc.

While the three-month figure was flat, monthly data showed a sharp increase at the end of the period. Unemployment jumped to 5.4pc in June, up from 4.6pc the previous month.

That marked the highest reading since October 2020 and the biggest monthly jump in 13 years.

Julian Jessop, at the Institute of Economic Affairs, described the latest jobs figures as “dire”.

He said: “The unemployment rate remains stubbornly high, with a big jump in the single month figure for June.”

It came as private sector wage growth slumped to a six-year low of just 2.8pc. That stands in contrast to a 6.1pc pay increase for the average public sector worker in the same period.

Meanwhile, vacancies dropped to 707,000 in the three months to July – the lowest level since 2021 – with a particular strain on entry-level job openings.

Ben Harrison, director of the Work Foundation at Lancaster University, warned that the UK was “trapped in a deepening jobs drought”.

Thomas Pugh, chief economist at RSM UK, said: “Stagnant, or even negative, real wage growth in the second half of this year will intensify the pressure on Burnham and Healey to come up with a package to support the cost of living.

“However, doing anything substantial without breaching either the fiscal rules or the manifesto commitments looks increasingly difficult given the deterioration in headroom and commitments to spend big on everything from defence to social care.”

Sports.title: Carlos Baleba could be set for shock position change under Michael Carrick once £65m Man Utd transfer is completed
Sports.content:
CARLOS BALEBA could be handed a shock new role under Michael Carrick if he completes his £65million move to Manchester United.

The Brighton star is closing in on an Old Trafford switch as Carrick looks to put the finishing touches to his squad.



And while Baleba is being brought in to bolster United’s midfield, he could provide an unlikely answer elsewhere if Carrick is left short over, especially with European football this season.

The 22-year-old is left-footed and has previously played at left-back, as well as filling in at centre-back.



Dream Team is back, free, and there’s £100,000 up for grabs!

It does not seem like United are signing him exclusively to be a left-back but he could pitch in if needed.

In 2024, Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler noted that he was up for using Baleba as another left-back option for the Seagulls.



Hurzeler told The Athletic: “He is an option to play there.

“Against the ball he is very athletic. He has good speed, he is good one-against-one and with the ball.

This dilemma comes after United flirted with a number of players this summer who can operate in both midfield and at left-back.

Arsenal’s Myles Lewis-Skelly was reportedly offered to the Red Devils by intermediaries earlier this month.

Sports.title: Crysencio Summerville’s panenka penalty goes horribly wrong as he is berated by team-mate after blunder
Sports.content:
CRYSENCIO SUMMERVILLE fumbled the chance to open his Al-Hilal account as his cheeky panenka went horribly wrong.

The £60million summer signing from West Ham was handed the chance to convert from 12 yards after the Saudi side were awarded a penalty while 2-0 up at Al-Fayha on Thursday night.



He took a deep breath and disguised his chipped attempt, with the keeper diving down to his right.

But Summerville overcooked the dink and, to his horror, the ball clipped the top of the crossbar and flew behind.



Dream Team is back, free, and there’s £100,000 up for grabs!

The Dutchman, 24, put his head in his hands and wiped his face with his jersey.

All the while he was getting a rollicking from team-mate Sergej Milinkovic-Savic, who was seen shouting and gesturing in his direction.



Summerville was subbed off four minutes later before Nasser Al Dawsari rounded off a comfortable 3-0 win in the 88th minute.

It has been a tough start for Summerville in Saudi, failing to contribute to any of the seven goals Al-Hilal have netted in his two appearances thus far.

The Saudi giants’ squad also includes Karim Benzema, Darwin Nunez, Joao Cancelo, Theo Hernandez, Kalidou Koulibaly and Ruben Neves.

So Summerville will have to produce if he is to stand out among that star-studded company.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Triple Man Utd deal, Liverpool's Endrick move, blockbuster Arsenal swap
Sports.content:
The latest transfer news and rumours from the Premier League and around the world as deadline day edges closer

Hello and welcome to the Mirror's live transfer blog on Friday, August 20.

The big news on Thursday was that Liverpool had a £50m bid for Yankuba Minteh rejected by Brighton & Hove Albion. The Reds have been scouring the market for wingers this summer and tabled an opening offer for the Gambia international after shortlisting him earlier this year.

However, while the player is believed to be keen on a move to Anfield, Liverpool’s offer falls short of Brighton’s valuation, and it remains to be seen whether the Reds will return with another offer.

Curtis Jones, meanwhile, is set to complete a move to Inter Milan in a transfer that could be worth £30million. He has had permission to fly to Italy to undergo a medical after a deal was agreed on Thursday.

While Manchester City are pursuing a deal for Palmeiras winger Allan, as Savinho remains in talks with Tottenham Hotspur. But one man who won’t be leaving his club this summer is Myles Lewis-Skelly, as Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta yesterday ruled out a transfer happening this summer.

The Gunners also continue to be linked with a move for Julian Alvarez from Atletico Madrid, with one report claiming a deal between the Spanish club and the Gunners had been agreed. Alvarez, though, still favours a move to Barcelona.

And Manchester United have reportedly contacted Barcelona to ask about Alejandro Balde's situation at the club. The Red Devils are keen to add a left-back to the squad this summer, and it is claimed that Barca are willing to listen to offers for Balde this summer.

We will keep you up to date on those moves and much more right here on our blog below...

Despite the 19-year-old's signing increasing competition going forwards, ESPN claims that Endrick wants to stay after enjoying training this summer. Mourinho is said to believe the forward can be a versatile attacking option.

Both the coach and player have apparently rejected offers from Aston Villa and Roma over recent weeks. After spending the second half of last season on loan at Lyon, Endrick has featured for Mourinho during pre-season this month.

The 20-year-old started and scored in his first outing of the summer against Fiorentina. Endrick also started their friendlies with Deportivo La Coruna and Ferencvaros, but did not feature last time out.

‌



View 2 Images Jose Mourinho reportedly values Endrick as a versatile attacking option for Real Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

Diomande made his non-competitive debut in Endrick's absence, replacing Brahim Diaz for the final half-hour. The former RB Leipzig winger has spoken highly of Mourinho since arriving in the Spanish capital.

In the same interview with SportyTV, he said: "As soon as I arrived, he told me: 'I promised you that you were going to be part of my team, and here you are.' And I told him: 'I'm happy to work with you because you are the best.'

‌



"I can learn a lot from him; he is the right coach to continue my development. I am prepared to die for him."

Sports.title: Four players could miss Arsenal vs Coventry as injury blows already confirmed
Sports.content:
Four players could miss Arsenal vs Coventry as injury blows already confirmed

Reigning champions Arsenal get their Premier League season underway tonight against Coventry City at the Emirates Stadium - but Mikel Arteta has a new fitness doubt

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta and Frank Lampard go head-to-head this evening as Arsenal host Coventry (Image: (David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

Mikel Arteta is sweating on the fitness of Bruno Guimaraes heading into tonight’s game against Coventry City. Arsenal begin the defence of their Premier League title against Frank Lampard’s side at the Emirates Stadium.

‌



Guimaraes, who joined the Gunners from Newcastle United earlier this month, was forced off during the Community Shield victory over Manchester City last weekend. And speaking on Thursday afternoon, Arteta admitted: "Let's see how it is, it's evolving well, but let's see for tomorrow."

‌



However, Arteta will be without defenders William Saliba and Jurrien Timber. Saliba is continuing his rehabilitation from a back injury sustained at the World Cup, while Timber remains sidelined with a long-term groin problem.

‌



“No, I said in the next few weeks,” Arteta said on Thursday when asked if Timber can join team training this week. “He's not training with the group yet.”

But there was better news for Gunners supporters, with Arteta confirming that Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka are fit to start against the Sky Blues. The Arsenal boss said: “Yes, they're ready to be involved, yes.”

Arsenal predicted XI vs Coventry City as Mikel Arteta faces selection dilemmas READ MORE :

While Frank Lampard confirmed on Thursday that Coventry will be without striker Haji Wright for the games against the Gunners. Wright was Coventry’s top scorer last season, scoring 17 times as his side won the Sky Bet Championship.

‌



The striker has been absent from recent friendly matches against RCD Espanyol and AS Monaco. And Lampard admitted his star man could be out for as long as 12 weeks. He said: “Haji Wright won’t be available for the Arsenal game.

“He won’t be available for a little while, he’s got a very serious quad injury which is disappointing for Haji and for us. It’s certainly going to be a number of weeks, could even be up to 12 weeks.”

Lampard, though, did confirm that both Ephron Mason-Clark and Jack Rudoni will be in contention to feature at the Emirates after they missed games in pre-season.

‌



View 2 Images Haji Wright won't be available for Coventry City (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The Coventry boss also admitted his side need to be ready for “tougher times” this season ahead of their Premier League curtain-raiser. He said: “We will go through tougher times this year for sure because of the competition we’re up against now so we’ll need resilience in moments calmness in moments.

‌



“An important part of my role is to have that balance and through having a long playing career through having a managerial career where I’ve had some really great moments and some difficult moments.

“But as a club we will need to stick together in those moments but I want to sound like I’m being too negative before something’s happened. It’s just a reality that we need to be ready for.

“Second spell at Chelsea wasn’t great for me, for a PR point. But having been through the challenges for good and for bad in my managerial career I think it puts me in a better spot to deal with – don’t get too high, don’t get too low – continue and focus on your.”

Sports.title: Tottenham set to sign Man City star Savinho as spending spree smashes £300m mark
Sports.content:
Tottenham set to sign Man City star Savinho as spending spree smashes £300m mark

Tottenham have spent heavily so far this summer following a dismal campaign and Roberto De Zerbi’s men are now set to raid Manchester City for two big-money signings

View 2 Images Spurs have agreed a deal to sign Savinho (Image: Getty Images)

Tottenham have agreed a deal worth up to £85m to sign Manchester City winger Savinho. The North London side are long-term admirers of the Brazilian winger, having failed to agree terms on a €50million (£43.3m) deal last summer.

‌



But they have retained their interest in the 22-year-old and are now close to finally securing his services. According to The Athletic, Spurs have agreed to pay £75m up-front for the former Troyes man, with £10m in potential bonuses.

‌



Should the deal go through as expected, it would represent a record sale for City, eclipsing the £81m sale of Julian Alvarez to Atletico Madrid in 2024.

‌



Savinho would also become the latest high-profile departure from the Etihad Stadium this summer, with Tijjani Reijnders, Rodri, James Trafford, Nathan Ake, Bernardo Silva and John Stones having all left alongside former boss Pep Guardiola.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The sales might not even be finished there, either. Spurs are also in talks with City over a deal for Egyptian forward Omar Marmoush.

‌



A deal for both him and Savinho is expected to cost around £140m - meaning Marmoush is valued at around £55m. The 27-year-old only joined City from Eintracht Frankfurt in January last year and has gone on to net 16 goals in 62 appearances.

Meanwhile, Savinho joined the club from French side Troyes in 2024 but has only netted twice in 53 Premier League outings.

Once their moves to North London are complete, they will become the latest arrivals in what has been an astonishing £369m rebuild under Roberto De Zerbi. Spurs have already signed Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Jan Paul van Hecke for big fees, while Marcos Senesi, Andrew Robertson and Martin Dubravka have all joined on free transfers.

‌



View 2 Images Omar Marmoush is expected to follow Savinho to North London (Image: Getty Images)

Spurs start their season against London rivals Brentford on Saturday evening, while Man City entertain Bournemouth on Sunday. Ahead of that game, City boss Enzo Maresca has already hinted that more signings could arrive before the deadline.

He said: "We knew already before the game the things that we need to do. It is not because we lost the game. We are quite clear. For sure, we are going to do something before the transfer window closes."

Article continues below

City have been linked with Lille star Ayyoub Bouaddi but the Italian remained tight-lipped on a deal. He added: "He is still a Lille player. But any new signing as soon as they arrive, it’s better [for us], because we have the Premier League starting in one week."

Sports.title: Arsenal predicted XI vs Coventry City as Mikel Arteta faces selection dilemmas
Sports.content:
Arsenal predicted XI vs Coventry City as Mikel Arteta faces selection dilemmas

Arsenal will kick off their Premier League title defence against newly-promoted Coventry City on Friday night and a few new signings could potentially be in line to appear for the Gunners

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta is aiming to guide Arsenal to a second, consecutive title (Image: Getty Images)

For the first time in over 20 years, Arsenal head into a Premier League season as defending champions. The North London side waltzed to their fourth title under the stewardship of Mikel Arteta last term, finally getting over the line after years of near misses.

‌



And while the celebrations of them hoisting the trophy at Selhurst Park back in May will be fresh in the minds of every player and fan, it’s now back down to business.

‌



Arsenal kick off the defence of their title on Friday night as they welcome newly-promoted Coventry City to the Emirates Stadium.

‌



Supporters have already managed to get a glimpse of the champions as they eased past Manchester City to win the Community Shield. New signings Christos Tzolis and Bruno Guimaraes were handed their debuts but did either of the pair do enough to start in Arsenal’s league opener?

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Before we answer that question, let’s start in defence where Gunners boss Mikel Arteta has a pretty simple task ahead of him. Last season’s Golden Glove winner David Raya will of course start between the sticks - and the defence in front of him effectively picks itself.

‌



Both William Saliba and Jurrien Timber are ruled out through injury, which opens the door to Cristhian Mosquera and Ben White. Brazilian centre-back Gabriel Magalhaes will partner the former in the heart of defence.

There’s then a debate to be had at the other fullback spot, where Riccardo Calafiori, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Piero Hincapie could all play. But given the Italian’s performance in the Community Shield, Arteta may just stick with what he already has.

Academy graduate Lewis-Skelly shone in Cardiff against City, so it feels very harsh to suggest that he could drop out. But Declan Rice is now fit and ready to go, Arteta did express some fitness doubts about new signing Bruno Guimaraes - but that's nothing new for the Gunners boss, he should still start.

‌



View 2 Images Declan Rice might start against Coventry (Image: Getty Images)

It’s also very difficult to envisage Arteta not starting captain Martin Odegaard for the Gunners’ Premier League opener.

When it comes to his attack, the Arsenal boss now has a wealth of options to choose from. Summer arrival Tzolis enjoyed a bright start to life with his new club in the Community Shield after notching two assists and that performance might well have been enough to earn a starting spot against Coventry.

‌



Noni Madueke started on the opposite flank against City, but Arteta might be tempted to draft in Bukayo Saka for a start.

There is then another debate to be had in the central attacking position, where Kai Havertz, Viktor Gyokeres and Gabriel Jesus are all options. The German scored against City - and appeared to have usurped Gyokeres in the pecking order at the end of last season - so is probably a good bet to start again.

Arsenal predicted XI vs Coventry: Raya; Calafiori, Gabriel, Mosquera, White; Rice, Guimaraes, Odegaard; Tzolis, Saka, Havertz.

Sports.title: Liverpool made to give up Premier League privilege as Arsenal reap rewards
Sports.content:
Liverpool made to give up Premier League privilege as Arsenal reap rewards

There will be notable difference to Arsenal's kit this season

View 2 Images Liverpool's loss has been Arsenal's gain (Image: PA)

Liverpool have been forced to give up a perk after relinquishing the Premier League title to Arsenal. The Gunners will begin a season as defending champions for the first time in 22 years when they host Coventry City on Friday, while Liverpool visit Newcastle on Sunday.

‌



Aside from introducing new kits, there will be a notable difference in the shirts of both sides compared to last season. The gold Premier League badge, which is added to the sleeve of the champions' shirt, has been removed from Liverpool's and handed to Arsenal.

‌



The gold badge was first added to the champions' kit for the 2015/16 season, meaning the Reds have had the honour twice, while the Gunners will enjoy the privilege for the first time. That privilege extends to the fans, who have been adding the patch to their own replica shirts in their droves since May.

‌



Following an impressive 3-0 victory over Manchester City in the Community Shield on Sunday, Mikel Arteta's side look well placed to retain the title and the coveted gold badge.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Arteta said the result and performance showed the Gunners are ready for the defence of their crown. He said: "The desire comes [because] I want to live that moment again.

‌



Arsenal chief makes transfer window vow as Mikel Arteta shortlist revealed READ MORE :

"I want to live other moments, even bigger than them. We know what it's going to take. We know the difficulty of the task.

"We've never done it at this club, to win it again. We know that it’s going to demand something special and we are ready for it."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



The Gunners are favourites to successfully defend their title, especially after putting down such an impressive marker against opponents expected to be their closest rivals.

Arteta added: "We talked about the desire we have to start the season and to show ourselves how much we want it, I saw a lot of positive things against a top opponent.

View 2 Images The gold badge that adorned Liverpool's shirt last season (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

"I am obviously extremely happy with the performance, the result, and winning the first trophy. I think it is down to the preparation we have done in pre-season.

"To the decisions the boys took after the World Cup, to continue to get prepared, to come early because they wanted to be part of it. If we drive the standards at this level, I’m sure that we’re going to be really, really competitive."

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Virgil van Dijk makes 'unacceptable' claim as club approve three transfer exits
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Virgil van Dijk makes 'unacceptable' claim as club approve three transfer exits

Liverpool are just days away from their Premier League opener against Newcastle United but the transfer window is still wide open

View 3 Images Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola is all set for his debut Premier League season at Anfield (Image: Getty)

Liverpool's Premier League curtain-raiser against Newcastle United is just around the corner. But Andoni Iraola's squad have only welcomed three new additions so far this summer.

‌



In his first season in charge, new manager Iraola, who has supplanted Arne Slot, will travel to St. James' Park on Sunday. But clubs have until September 1 to conclude their transfer business.

‌



Victor Munoz (£34.6million), Jeremy Jacquet (£60m) and Ronald Araujo (loan with a £47.1m purchase option) complete the Reds' incomings. But with Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson departing, some feel there is still a lot to be done.

‌



However, another exit has been confirmed and two more are on the cards as Mirror Football brings you all the latest transfer updates from Anfield.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool receive Brighton response after launching £50m Yankuba Minteh transfer bid READ MORE :

Reds allow three to leave

Liverpool have allowed young attacker Kieran Morrison to join Sheffield Wednesday on loan for the 2026/27 season. He will be followed out of the door by Calvin Ramsay and Ifeanyi Ndukwe.

‌



View 3 Images Morrison has joined Sheffield Wednesday (Image: Getty)

Morrison is 19 and signed a new Reds contract in May. He made his full international debut for Northern Ireland in June. Ramsay has played sparingly since joining Liverpool from Aberdeen in 2022 and has spent time with Preston, Bolton, Wigan and Kilmarnock since.

‌



Now, reports suggest he is all set to sign for St. Mirren on loan. He is out of contract next summer, meaning his Reds career could effectively be over. Ndukwe, the final departing star, impressed hugely in pre-season.

However, work permit issues mean the 18-year-old centre-back cannot play senior football yet for the Reds. Therefore, he is being shipped out on loan to Spanish side Levante and he has jetted in ahead of a move to La Liga, where he will play until at least January.

Virgil van Dijk makes demand

Elsewhere, Virgil van Dijk will begin the season with a new centre-back partner now that Ibrahima Konate has joined Real Madrid. Either Jacquet or Araujo will start next to him, but he has spoken out ahead of the campaign, demanding more from his team-mates and the new signings.

‌

Sports.title: Spurs agree £85m deal to sign Savinho from Man City
Sports.content:
Tottenham Hotspur have agreed an £85m deal with Manchester City to sign Savinho.

Spurs will pay an initial £75m for the Brazil international, with a further £10m available in add-ons.

It is understood that £5m of the potential bonuses are effectively guaranteed, meaning City could receive at least £80m from the deal.

The 22-year-old is scheduled to have a medical with Tottenham on Friday afternoon.

Spurs also remain in talks with Man City over a separate deal for striker Omar Marmoush as they look to further strengthen their attacking options.

Brentford

Tottenham Hotspur Saturday 22nd August 5:00pm Kick off 5:30pm

Savinho, who has played a bit-part role since joining Manchester City in 2024, started only seven of his 24 Premier League appearances last season, in which he scored once and set up two goals.

Tottenham have already spent more than £200m on six first-team players this summer. They spent £185m on two midfielders, Sandro Tonali and Matheus Fernandes, from Newcastle and West Ham respectively.

Jan Paul van Hecke joined from Brighton for £52m to replace Cristian Romero.

Marcos Senesi, Andy Robertson and Martin Dubravka all arrived on free transfers.

How are Spurs spending so much money?

At the start of the transfer window, Sky Sports News' Michael Bridge explained how Spurs are able to spend big this summer...

"We're told there are absolutely no concerns about falling foul of the Premier League's financial rules.

"The club is in great financial health after qualifying for Europe in 18 of the last 20 seasons. The revenue driven by the stadium is huge: boxing, concerts, NFL games - you name it.

"In fact, in the Deloitte Money League, the rankings show that Tottenham Hotspur have leapfrogged Chelsea to become the ninth richest club in the world with annual revenues of £549.2m.

"On top of that, Spurs are one of the clubs to benefit most from the Premier League's shift to squad cost ratio from PSR, which has just come into effect. But the reason we're seeing Spurs spend so much is a shift in strategy under new leadership.

"Daniel Levy left at the start of last season, and there's a real desire to spend the money to dine at the very top table.

"Now the new leadership and the owners promised fans, after avoiding relegation on the final day, that they would spend the club's revenue on the first team, and they are delivering on that."

'City will want to replace Savinho and Marmoush'

Sky Sports News' Ben Ransom:

"Both players [Savinho and Marmoush] are essentially surplus to requirements at Manchester City. It's been pretty apparent through the summer. Enzo Maresca has said that in the case of both players, they are very much entitled to stay and fight for their first-team place.

Manchester City

Bournemouth Sunday 23rd August 1:00pm Kick off 2:00pm

"But equally he understands, a bit like James Trafford, when a player wants to play first-team football and they're not guaranteed the starting shirt, then the club, if they receive an offer that's acceptable, will not stand in their way. That applies to both players.

"City would need to replace these players. They would definitely, I'd say, have to replace one. They would like to and would aim to replace two.

"But the transfer window is closing in less than a fortnight. These are big positions to fill so late in the window."

Sports.title: Hadjar hopeful of Italian GP return after wrist injury
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar is hopeful he can return for the next Formula 1 race after a wrist injury forced him to miss this weekend's Dutch Grand Prix.

Hadjar suffered the injury while boxing in training during the summer break earlier this month and will be replaced by Liam Lawson, who becomes the first driver to race again for Red Bull having previously being dropped by the team.

Yuki Tsunoda will take over Lawson's seat at Racing Bulls alongside full-time driver Arvid Lindblad.

Sky Sports News understands Hadjar suffered a small crack in a bone in his wrist late last week in a routine workout before discussions with Red Bull medical staff led to the decision to miss the Sprint weekend at Zandvoort to allow more time for recovery before the next race at Monza.

Hadjar is at the track this weekend at Zandvoort to support Lawson and is hopeful of a return at the Italian Grand Prix, which takes place on September 4-6.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hadjar tells Karun Chandhok he's pleased with how he's performed alongside Max Verstappen at Red Bull

Lawson: I'm much more comfortable compared to 18 months ago

Lawson was dropped from Red Bull after two disappointing races last year but did enough over the remainder of the 2025 season at Racing Bulls to retain his seat for this year.

The 24-year-old has been one of the stars in the midfield this season with eight points finishes and sits ninth in the Drivers' Championship - only behind the Mercedes, McLaren, Ferrari and Red Bull drivers.

"I've had a lot more races since then [being dropped from Red Bull]. I feel much more comfortable racing in this sport, but it's going to be a very challenging weekend, for sure," said Lawson.

"It's a Sprint weekend, so it's going to be a quick learning process. But that's what we're focused on, that's what we tried to do in the simulator. If we can try and speed up that learning process as much as possible, then that would help our weekend."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lawson sits down with Sky Sports F1's Crofty to reveal his the tracks he'd take with him to a desert island

Tsunoda has been watching from the sidelines this year and has an opportunity to impress to find a seat on the grid in 2027, albeit his options appear to be limited following the recent re-signings of Verstappen at Red Bull plus Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon at Williams.

The Japanese driver revealed he was on holiday in Greece before getting a call on Tuesday to get ready to drive for Racing Bulls.

"When I heard, I was like half excited, half still doubtful because anything can happen, but I was super excited too," he said.

"It was all confirmed that I'm racing this weekend. I'm super excited and physically I'm feeling ready. I've done a couple of TPCs [Testing of Previous Cars]. It will be my first time in this car but still, I'm very excited.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Yuki Tsunoda admits he feels excited, but 'half doubtful' about the pressure of stepping up into the RB seat for the Dutch Grand Prix

"As far as I understand, I will be in the seat for now - this weekend - and also it depends on Isack's recovery. I hope that recovery goes pretty fast. I'm not sure about the next Grand Prix but my objective is to have fun. I've been waiting for a long time. I was watching the screen for the last few months.

"Since the season started, I've been dying to be in the car and compete with the drivers. This moment I will just enjoy, and obviously give my 100 per cent performance. Hopefully that will bring some good results."

Sports.title: Sixtygeesbaby and Safari Dream lock horns at Ffos Las
Sports.content:
We have a busy day’s racing on Friday with flat action from Ffos Las, live on Sky Sports Racing...

2.10 Ffos Las - Recent winners Sixtygeesbaby and Safari Dream headline

The opening Ascona Ladies Fuelled By Fashion Handicap is a belter where Sixtygeesbaby and Safari Dream headline six runners.

Sixtygeesbaby had been showing signs of a revival on his last few starts before claiming a Carlisle handicap earlier this month and a similar effort would put him in the mix.

Safari Dream looks an obvious threat for Rod Millman and Finley Marsh. Rated much higher in the past, he bounced back to winning form over this course and distance and makes plenty of appeal despite a two-pound rise.

Pull The Rug could be the pick of the remainder.

3.20 Ffos Las - Korbut, Likeness and Reader seek elusive first victory

A trappy affair with just the three runners for this Ascona Ladies In Lace Maiden Stakes at 3.20pm.

Korbut has claimed silver on five of her seven starts including the last four runs this summer. Rated 73, she should make a bold bid if able to reproduce her latest run back on the turf.

Marcus Tregoning saddles Reader who has a little to find of official figures but is lightly raced and may have more to give over this extra distance.

Sports.title: Why a German football superstar is now playing in the third tier
Sports.content:
"Not normal." It is a phrase that Alexandra Popp turns to more than once when speaking after her debut for Borussia Dortmund. She has scored twice. The team has won 3-0. Nothing unusual there. But the crowd of 4,572 in Germany's third tier is new.

Popp is already a phenomenon here. The average attendance at Dortmund last season was below half the number at the atmospheric Stadion Rote Erde for this game against Arminia Bielefeld. Season ticket sales have almost tripled from 600 to 1700.

It is because Popp has come. This summer, the former captain of the Germany national team with 67 international goals to her name joined the club she supported as a girl. It is a homecoming that has captured the imagination among her fellow fans.

Image: Popp's Borussia Dortmund shirt is outselling many of the men

Her shirt is everywhere in Dortmund and not just among the growing fanbase for the women's team. Sales of the shirt that bears her name are currently outselling those of Serhou Guirassy, the top scorer for the men's team for each of the past two seasons.

Speaking to Popp after her match-winning display, she says: "It was a very nice atmosphere. We have more than 4,000 people here in the stadium and that is amazing. I played for so many years in the Bundesliga and some stadiums are not so full like that."

It is some transformation because Dortmund did not even have a women's team until 2020, by which point Popp was already a three-time champion of Europe and a six-time Bundesliga winner. Having started in the seventh tier, the club are now up to the third.

Image: Fans look on during the women's match between Borussia Dortmund and Arminia Bielefeld

In truth, the football is far beneath her level. When a cross was hung up into the penalty box late in the first half and Popp attacked the ball with her head, the outcome was as inevitable as watching Erling Haaland up against children. She was utterly unstoppable.

But this was an emotional move for a 35-year-old icon motivated by more than just the standard of football. "I had two choices," she explains. "To stay in Wolfsburg or switch to my favourite kid as a club, Borussia Dortmund. The decision did not take long."

Popp has a reputation for being a relatively stoical figure, a determined soul known for her drive and determination. But she admits the reaction to her arrival has been overwhelming. "It is wonderful. You see the heart of the club and the heart of the fans."

Image: Popp's move to Dortmund has captured the imagination

The chance to inspire is another reason for coming home. "I can develop something here." It was something of an embarrassment that the best supported team in European men's football did not have a women's team. They are trying to make up for lost time.

"It is a new challenge for me," she says. And for all her superiority, on this evidence, it might not be completely straightforward. "It was a tough game," she concedes. Arminia offered dogged resistance and Popp had to endure some particularly robust treatment.

"Some people told me before that it is possible I get some fouls. It is what it is." Two opposition players were booked for fouling Popp and it could and should have been many more. She tried to counter this by roaming all over the pitch in search of space.

Image: Popp speaking to reporters after scoring two goals on her Dortmund debut

"Everywhere," she replies, laughing, when asked by Sky Sports what position she was supposed to be playing in. "No, I have to play on the 10. But I am a player when I see there is some space or we need to defend or something, I take my legs and I run back."

Another consideration is how her mere presence at the club changes the dynamic for young team-mates who are unaccustomed to the world's media turning up at the old ground next to the cavernous Signal-Iduna Park that hosts the men's team.

Image: Popp is covering the ground for the team

"Some of them were a bit nervous," says Popp. There is Manuela Zinsberger, the former Bayern Munich and Arsenal goalkeeper, who on the evidence of this game is not likely to be too busy this season. But many others are living a new experience right now.

"We have a normal relationship," insists Popp. "The young girls speak with me all the time. They are not scared and that is very important. Sometimes even in the national team, the young girls are scared to tell me something. The girls here are very open."

Image: Popp during a public training session

Even without Popp, Dortmund had a goal difference of over 100 last season, somehow contriving not to win promotion as they missed out on top spot by two points - both of which were dropped in this corresponding fixture against Arminia last season in April.

This time around, it is unlikely to be an issue. Popp and Dortmund have big ambitions. "That is the first, the championship," she says. "I hope that we can make more steps. We have a dream to grow. We want to be in the first league as fast as we can."

And with that, Germany's three-time footballer of the year is off. There are autographs to sign, fans of all ages demanding selfies. Popp has signed a three-year contract. By then, the aim is to be back in the Bundesliga where she belongs. But Alex Popp is already home.

Sports.title: Uefa and Concacaf discuss joint Nations League in latest challenge to Fifa
Sports.content:
Uefa and Concacaf have begun talks about setting up a combined Nations League tournament featuring all 96 European and North and Central American and Caribbean countries, in another direct challenge to Fifa.

The Guardian has learned that having come together to push for Gianni Infantino’s removal in the light of the World Cup sell-off controversy, the two confederations are now working on creating their own biennial tournament, which could launch as early as 2028 after the next European Championship.

Although discussions are at an early stage, it is understood the new competition would mirror the current multi-league format used for the existing Nations Leagues by Europe’s governing body and Concacaf, the Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football. It would be followed by a knockout phase, a final-four tournament to determine the champions.

League A would feature the top teams in Europe, including Spain, France, England and Germany, playing competitive league fixtures against the highest-ranked nations in Concacaf such as Mexico, the United States and Canada.

Uefa and Concacaf launched Nations League competitions in 2018, with the confederations staging fixtures in the same international windows, so the mechanics required to set up a joint tournament are already in place.

Under the draft plans the league phase would be played during the existing September, October and November international breaks, followed by knockout matches in March and finals in June.

As the fixtures would take place during international windows that have already been agreed, it is unclear whether the new tournament would need to be ratified by Fifa, although given the world governing body is in the midst of an existential crisis with Infantino facing a leadership challenge that may be a moot point.

With serious discussions having begun only in the last few weeks, the number of teams in each league has yet to be determined, but all 96 members of Uefa and Concacaf would be involved and much of the revenue pooled, generating significant additional income for smaller nations.

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino is under pressure with Uefa and Concacaf pushing for his removal and now planning a combined Nations League tournament. Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA

The commercial appeal of the bigger European teams playing regular competitive matches in North America and Canada would be considerable, while there would also be major benefits for Mexico, whose football federation (FMF) is known to be frustrated by what it sees as the financial limitations of playing within Concacaf.

The FMF has held initial discussions about leaving to join the South American confederation, Conmebol, in a move that would need to be ratified by Fifa, but the prospect of lucrative matches against European opposition could lead to a change of heart.

The proposed new format would replace rather than add to existing international fixtures, while games would be played in geographic blocks to reduce travel.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) is also understood to have expressed interest in joining a global Nations League at a future date, and the competition structure being discussed would be flexible enough to accommodate them. The AFC does not currently operate a Nations League, however, so that would be a more long-term aspiration.

Uefa and Concacaf have been working together for some time, and signed a memorandum of understanding to promote greater cooperation at Fifa’s congress in Vancouver in April, but have become even more closely aligned since the World Cup sell-off plan emerged last month.

Both confederations have made it abundantly clear that they regard Infantino’s position as untenable as a result of his role in the Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal, and are working together to propose an alternative candidate to stand against him in the presidential election next March.

Uefa declined to comment, although one source with knowledge of the proposal confirmed discussions are under way.

Concacaf declined to comment directly, but highlighted the confederation’s longstanding commitment to collaboration, which has led to guest teams participating in the Concacaf Gold Cup.

A historically strong relationship with Conmebol has resulted in many South American teams taking part in the Gold Cup, as have South Africa, South Korea, Saudi Arabia and Qatar.

Sports.title: Tottenham close on deals for Manchester City’s Savinho and Omar Marmoush
Sports.content:
Manchester City are close to agreeing the transfer of Savinho to Tottenham for £85m, with a separate deal of around £75m for the arrival of Omar Marmoush from the FA Cup-winners to the north London club also being worked on.

Savinho signed for the City Football Group in summer 2022 for 40m euros (£30.8m), first joining Troyes, so the prospective sale of the 22-year-old for £85m represents a near £55m profit for City’s owners. After loans at PSV and Girona, the Brazilian joined City two years ago but the winger failed to establish himself as a first-choice under Pep Guardiola, the former manager.

Marmoush was bought in January 2025 for around £59m but, as with Savinho, the Egyptian forward was not a regular starter under Guardiola, due to having to compete with Erling Haaland.

If Spurs do buy both Savinho and Marmoush, that would take the club’s investment in Roberto De Zerbi’s squad this summer to £387m, after the purchases of Sandro Tonali for £100m, Mateus Fernandes (£85m), and Jan Paul van Hencke (£52m).

Sports.title: PSG are the best team in Europe. The rest of Ligue 1 are just trying to survive
Sports.content:
On the eve of a new Ligue 1 season, many clubs seem a little distracted. Even those accustomed to competing at the top have concerns that transcend the pitch. In a league that contains the greatest team on the continent, the focus of the majority of clubs has shifted to surviving and providing, rather than competing.

Any fighting spirit has long since been kicked out of Paris Saint-Germain’s competitors; back-to-back Champions League titles will do that. It feels like a long time ago since Kylian Mbappé moved to Real Madrid on a free transfer, leaving behind a scent of opportunity that filled the nostrils of Marseille, Monaco and Lille. Roberto De Zerbi was bullish when he joined Marseille. “I’m not here to finish second,” said the manager, who has since moved to Tottenham. Finishing second has now become an aspiration, especially for a club such as Marseille, given their predicament.

Of all of the distracted teams, Marseille are the most preoccupied with off-field matters. While the club avoided a European ban, allowing them to compete in the Europa League this season, Uefa’s tone was one of a final warning: redress the financial imbalance or you’re out.

There has been a change in the dugout, with the (almost boringly) dependable Bruno Génésio coming in for Habib Beye, who replaced De Zerbi in February, but the demands made by Uefa – and the DNCG, French football’s financial watchdog – have prevented the club from making a single signing. There have been plenty of sales (Mason Greenwood, Facundo Medina, Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Gérnoimo Rulli have all left on permanent deals), but not enough for Marseille to contemplate dipping into the market themselves.

Marseille’s “everything must go” sale suggested the club were in survival mode and their reaction to Pierre-Emile Højbjerg refusing a move to Newcastle confirmed it. He was stripped of the captaincy for the club’s friendly against Atlético Madrid. Génésio said it was a decision made above his station and one he disagreed with. “I am an employee. I have to agree to certain obligations,” he said.

View image in fullscreen Pierre-Emile Højbjerg was stripped of the captaincy for Marseille’s friendly against Atlético Madrid. Photograph: Icon Sport/Alamy Stock Photo/Alamy Live News.

Génésio wants to keep Højbjerg, but the austerity cure ensures the club are hell-bent on doing the opposite. It is a situation that perfectly encapsulates the conflict between sporting ambition and financial necessity, familiar to many clubs in Ligue 1, and increasingly those competing towards the top of it – lest we forget Lyon’s recent brush with administration.

With the authorities “supervising their wage bill”, Monaco have made savings this summer. Maghnes Akliouche’s £43m move to PSG has been programmed for some time, and Folarin Balogun and Lamine Camara may still bring in big fees before the end of the window. The unexpected sale of Aladji Bamba to Newcastle for £34m has given the club more breathing room in their quest to cut costs and raise funds.

TV broadcasting rights are no longer the lifeblood of Ligue 1. Instead, French clubs rely on the reckless abandon of Premier League sides making multimillion-pound bets on unproven young players. Bamba had played 18 league games when Newcastle came with the big money. Ligue 1 has always been a ​stopover for its top talents, but the rate of churn has hit new levels. Liverpool did not wait around before signing Jérémy Jacquet and Mamadou Sangaré only needed one campaign at Lens to convince Brentford he was worth an expensive bet.

Even those in stronger financial health cannot resist advances. The prospect of coaching Lens in the Champions League could not prevent Pierre Sage from crossing the Channel to join Crystal Palace. Sangaré made a similar journey, while Adrien Thomasson, Malang Sarr, Allan Saint-Maximin and Wesley Saïd – all instrumental in Lens’ second-place finish and maiden Coupe de France triumph last season – have been lured away. Success can be a poisoned chalice. At least their rebuild, under Dino Toppmöller, looks intelligent. You’d expect nothing less from Lens, but their pillaging once again exposes the limits to success in Ligue 1 for clubs that do not go by the name PSG.

View image in fullscreen Allan Saint-Maximin celebrates after scoring for Lens in the Coupe de France semi-final against Toulouse. He has now moved to MLS. Photograph: Benoît Tessier/Reuters

The reigning champions, who are in search of a sixth consecutive league title, have often been accused of being distracted by the Champions League. When you win it two years in a row, you can justify it, but after their close race with Lens last season it isn’t an accusation that can be levelled at them this summer. Their starting XI is already the best in the league and beyond, so PSG’s transfer guru, Luís Campos, has focused on improving the second string that more often than not will be trotted out in Ligue 1.

Ferran Torres, Akliouche and Mika Godts are upgrades on the departing trio of Gonçalo Ramos, Lee Kang-in and Randal Kolo Muani, even if they will struggle to dislodge the current starters in the PSG attack. Lucas Digne is a shrewd pick as back-up to Nuno Mendes, too.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

PSG will probably have an easier ride in the league this season as the teams chasing them have either regressed or stagnated. Rennes, who must this season contend with European football for the first time in three seasons, are the only side that finished in the top seven last season that – on paper – look stronger than they were at the start of the summer.

Wealth immunises Rennes, to a degree, but Strasbourg are weaker after losing important players to Chelsea. Emanuel Emegha, the club captain, has been followed out the door by Valentín Barco, with the goalkeeper Mike Penders returning to his parent club after a loan spell at the Meinau. The latter has been replaced by Filip Jörgensen, who will have to play a “crucial role”, in the words of their new manager, Hugo Oliveira, formerly assistant to Marco Silva at Fulham. Time will tell if Jörgensen is up to the task; he was surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge so it may be a move born out of convenience. In any case, he will be busy if pre-season is anything to go by; Strasbourg have conceded 21 goals in their seven friendlies.

The managerial upheaval, from Liam Rosenior to Gary O’Neil, and now to Oliveira, also contributes to a feeling of instability at Strasbourg, one of 10 clubs part of a multi-club model in Ligue 1 this season. That, in itself, adds a feeling of “Who is this even for?” to the upcoming season. Not all clubs in these models are subservient, but nor do their own interests always guide decisions.

Rosenior knows all about that. The new Paris FC manager is one of two coaches returning to France in search of redemption following failed stints in England, with the former Southampton head coach Will Still joining Auxerre. There are also some more adventurous appointments, in the form of Davide Ancelotti at Lille and Filipe Luís at Monaco. There have been an incredible 12 managerial changes in France’s top flight for this season: plenty of change, even if some things will almost certainly stay the same.

This is an article by Get French Football News

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for as the new season kicks off
Sports.content:
1 Nwaneri out of Arsenal picture

While Myles Lewis-Skelly looks likely to remain at the Emirates, the same can’t be said for Ethan Nwaneri. The 19-year-old was outstanding in his breakthrough season for Arsenal in 2024-25 but barely featured last season and was sent on loan to Marseille. That didn’t really work out and Arsenal are now exploring another temporary move to ensure Nwaneri gets regular football this season. Milan, RB Leipzig, Dortmund and Fulham are all thought to be interested, with Nwaneri unlikely to feature on the bench for Friday’s opener against Coventry as a result. Whether Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus are available remains to be seen as Arsenal attempt to find suitors for the Brazil duo. Ed Aarons

Arsenal v Coventry City, Friday 8pm (all times BST)

2 New United pair down for Tigers test

Manchester United’s summer transfer business has focused on recruiting in central midfield. It will be interesting to see who Michael Carrick selects in two key roles for the first game of the season. Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have been present for more of pre-season than Kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute for England at the World Cup and was a late returner to Carrington after a holiday. Carlos Baleba surely will not have arrived in time to start at Hull. Mainoo is in the best position in the long term but if Carrick decides to ease him into the season, it would be intriguing to see how Santos and Tielemans team up, the stress test for a new partnership that could provide the perfect balance of defensive awareness and ability to move the team up the pitch. Will Unwin

Hull City v Manchester United, Saturday 12.30pm

3 Swapped pair face former clubs

Neither Everton nor Crystal Palace have enjoyed a particularly scintillating summer of transfer activity but combined to make headlines with a swap deal between Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson. The pair will face one another – and their former clubs - on the first weekend of the season, eager to prove what their worth to their new teams. McNeil was rarely a regular on Merseyside but had a positive second half to last season, ironically after a move to Crystal Palace fell through at the last minute. Johnson did not settle at Selhurst Park, unable to crack the code that would get him into the starting lineup on a weekly basis, after moving from Spurs. A fresh start should reinvigorate the duo and there is no better way to further boost the mood than beating a former employer. WU

Everton v Crystal Palace, Saturday 3pm

4 Can Ipswich copy Black Cats’ success?

Ipswich clearly learned a lot from what Sunderland did a year ago, as they went out and bought a lot of players. The Black Cats quickly moulded their 19 acquisitions into a successful unit but at least they had the positive of a head coach in Régis Le Bris who had his feet under the table. Gary O’Neil is the new man at Portman Road and he has 12 signings – at time of writing – to potentially use for the opener. The record arrival, Emersonn, who has moved to Portman Road from Toulouse, is the most eye-catching of those who have been acquired. The Brazilian has an underwhelming career goalscoring record and a few question marks hanging over his head. Even though it is their first game, Ipswich need to pick up points at home, and to do so require a striker who can cause problems for defenders. How quickly Emersonn adapts will be critical for the Tractor Boys’ success this year. WU

Ipswich Town v Sunderland, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen Emersonn is one of a number of big-money signings made by promoted Ipswich this summer. Photograph: Keeran Marquis/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

5 Glasner’s tough Diomande ready for debut

August is the season for debuts and no one will be more satisfied than Oliver Glasner when Ousmane Diomande steps over the white line at the City Ground. Glasner wanted the Ivorian centre-back to replace Marc Guéhi at Crystal Palace, six months before the England defender departed for Manchester City. Diomande, a £34m buy from Sporting, is expected to line up in a back three for Nottingham Forest against Leeds, when the Austria midfielder Xaver Schlager, who played for Glasner at Wolfsburg, could also make his Forest bow. Diomande is a quick and physical defender but another aspect of his appeal is his aerial power at set pieces. “They’ve both played Champions League football and they are used to competing for titles,” said Glasner. “They can add this winning mentality.” Ben Fisher

Nottingham Forest v Leeds, Saturday 3pm

6 Serene Senesi can bring calm to Spurs

Cristian Romero has taken his maverick brand of defending to Atlético Madrid, upsetting neutral Premier League watchers. His compatriot Marcos Senesi has arrived to shore up things at the back as Roberto De Zerbi desperately tries to steer Spurs away from a third straight season of battling relegation. The all-action Romero had his qualities as a leader and defender but never felt dependable, which is what most want from a centre-back and captain. Senesi impressed during his time at Bournemouth, rarely making headlines but proving himself a calm presence at the back. The Argentinian is good on the ball and will be more adventurous in possession than his countryman. He is yet to be sent off in three seasons as a Premier League player – Romero was dismissed twice in 2025-26 alone, not to mention a one-match ban and a fine for his behaviour towards a referee. His calmness will improve Spurs. WU

Brentford v Tottenham, Saturday 5.30pm

7 Villa head south besieged by problems

It is surely not how Unai Emery envisaged the countdown to Aston Villa’s season-opener at Brighton on Sunday – and certainly not as he enjoyed the afterglow from the club’s Europa League triumph over Freiburg in May. The manager has an extraordinary number of problems. Take the midfield where the new signings João Gomes and Johan Manzambi are injury doubts. Note: Amadou Onana is a long-term casualty while Youri Tielemans has been sold. It goes on. Emery is about to lose Ezri Konsa to Arsenal – in a summer where Villa have also sold Morgan Rogers and Lucas Digne. They are trying to move on Emi Martínez, while the future of Ollie Watkins is uncertain, with Al-Hilal circling. For the cherry on top, the rampaging 17-year-old striker Brian Madjo is a fitness concern. Emery’s teamsheet will be very interesting. Will he pitch the new goalkeeper, Zion Suzuki, who only signed on Wednesday, straight in? David Hytner

Brighton v Aston Villa, Sunday 2pm

8 Maresca must win to silence City noise

Is Enzo Maresca already under pressure after Manchester City’s 3-0 schooling by Arsenal in the Community Shield? Maybe not, but if the Italian’s new team go down at home to Bournemouth on Sunday, you do not have to be a soothsayer to picture the scrutiny that will follow. Maresca and City are enduring a difficult transfer window, with Rodri’s departure to Barcelona the headline, a dizzying blow that has to be shaken off. The new Bournemouth coach, Marco Rose, has faced City six times in the Champions League with Leipzig and Mönchengladbach, and is sure to order his visitors to go for the jugular at the Etihad. City are vulnerable but Maresca can remedy this with a win of any sort. This, after all, is the job many felt he was the obvious choice for. Jamie Jackson

Manchester City v Bournemouth, Sunday 2pm

View image in fullscreen Anything but a win for Manchester City at home to Bournemouth will increase scrutiny on Enzo Maresca. Photograph: Dimitris Legakis/EPA

9 King Kev remembered at Newcastle

Kevin Keegan was supposed to have been the guest of honour at St James’ Park on Sunday, but his death from cancer in July means this meeting of two of his old clubs will turn into a tribute to one of English football’s enduring heroes. Keegan’s family will be present to witness an outpouring of love for the former Liverpool and Newcastle forward and (twice) Magpies manager. Once the game kicks off, all eyes will be on Alexander Isak, a St James’ Park old boy whose decision to force a £125m move to Anfield last summer did not go down well on Tyneside. The Sweden striker, making his first return to Newcastle, has much to prove at Liverpool, and now has a new head coach to impress in Andoni Iraola. Newcastle too have a new face in the home dugout, where Matthias Jaissle will occupy the technical area for so long inhabited by Eddie Howe. Louise Taylor

Newcastle v Liverpool, Sunday 4.30pm

10 Former Madrid managers meet in capital

Real Madrid’s two head coaches from last season meet at Craven Cottage, with the focus on Xabi Alonso, rather than Álvaro Arbeloa. The Fulham man, however, may have more to prove in the Premier League. His managerial career has been less prominent than that of his Basque rival – and he has clearly insisted on snapping up talent from the Bernabéu. Gonzalo García and César Palacios have made the trip over from the Spanish capital with Arbeloa. It shows great faith from the former Liverpool defender but it does put extra pressure on the trio, their fates now permanently intertwined. All three need a positive start to show they merit being in the Premier League. Otherwise, it would be very easily to criticise them individually and collectively. WU

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Endrick to Liverpool? Arsenal to swap Martinelli for Yildiz?
Sports.content:
After Vinícius Júnior signed a shiny new deal at Real Madrid, Arsenal are having to look elsewhere for a new winger. Turkey’s Kenan Yildizm who plies his trade with Juventus, is of interest to Mikel Arteta and the Gunners hierarchy. One potential way of getting the deal done is to send Gabriel Martinelli in the opposite direction.

It is all fun and games at Manchester City where they are trying to rebuild a midfield inside a week. Adam Wharton is supposedly on their wishlist but with a £100m price tag, the expense could be a little too much. City have reportedly put in a call to Selhurst Park but received a swift rebuffing in response. Considering the proximity of that Sainsbury’s to the Palace ground, any potential purchase of a midfielder would come with a lot of Nectar points. With Savinho on his way to Tottenham, City could replace him with Allan Elias, a left-footed right winger at Palmeiras – a team not keen on selling. Ruben Amorim is eager on a return to Manchester but only to take Rúben Dias to Milan.

Over at Anfield there are plans afoot for Liverpool to bid £55m for Endrick to test Real Madrid’s mettle on the matter. The Brazilian spent time on loan at Lyon last season and was recently linked with Aston Villa, who could re-enter the race should Ollie Watkins head to Al-Hilal.

There is still a good chance of a Chelsea clearout, with Nicolas Jackson chatting with Napoli over a move to Italy, while Atlético Madrid are also keen. Palace are in the market for a centre-back and are keen on signing up Blues bomb squad member Axel Disasi. The Frenchman is unwanted at Stamford Bridge, so would be a relatively straightforward signing after previous loan spells with Aston Villa and West Ham. Auxerre’s Kevin Danois is another player Pierre Sage likes the look of, with the 22-year-old midfielder marketed at £25m.

On thing that could sour the mood at Selhurst Park is the departure of frontman Jean-Philippe Mateta who is getting admiring glances from Tottenham. The Frenchman has been tipped to move on for a while and is into the final year of his contract, which could force Palace to cash in.

The latest news from Hull’s transfer tombola has linked them to Oussama Targhalline of Feyenoord. A bid has already been faxed to the Netherlands but Porto, Atalanta and Bologna are also in in pursuit of the midfielder.

Leeds, Liverpool and Everton are in the hat for Midtjylland winger Darío Osorio. The Chilean shown great promise in Denmark and the Europa League, and could become one of the finds of the window if someone stumps the cash. If you like a bit of niche on your bingo card, then Polish side Radomiak Radom having a loan offer for Leeds youngster Alfie Cresswell rejected is right up there.

Sports.title: New rules, managers and pundits: what’s different this Premier League season?
Sports.content:
The 2026-27 Premier League season kicks off on Friday and while the familiar rivalries return, the English top flight has some alterations this campaign. From evolved rules to new faces and broadcast changes, there is plenty to catch up on before a ball is kicked.

Law changes

The Premier League has some law and rule changes this season and the first will lead to a crackdown on time wasting.

Referees will be able to start a countdown of five seconds if they believe players are ticking down the clock during throw-ins and goal-kicks. If players take more than five seconds once the countdown has been enforced, the goal-kick becomes a corner and the throw-in is reversed.

That is not all that is being done to cut time-wasting. Last season, if a player was injured and play stopped as a result, they had to leave the pitch for 30 seconds. In this campaign, it will be increased to a minute and the only exceptions will be if a foul that received a card led to the injury, or other unusual circumstances.

There will also be a change to limit tactical timeouts by goalkeepers going down injured. If they do, a manager must choose another player to leave the pitch for one minute. Substitutions will also need to take just 10 seconds; if a player takes longer than that to leave the pitch, his replacement will not be able to come on for a further minute.

There will also be changes to video assistant referee interventions. VARs will now be able to intervene on second yellow cards if they have been shown in error. They cannot, however, tell a referee to issue a second yellow if one is not shown.

VARs will also be able to get involved where an attacking foul happens before a set piece is taken which leads to a penalty, a goal or a disciplinary sanction. They will be able to intervene to have the set piece retaken.

Despite players being given red cards for speaking to opposition players with their mouths covered at the World Cup this past summer, this is not a rule that will be adopted by the Premier League.

Managerial appointments

View image in fullscreen Xabi Alonso at Chelsea is one of nine new managers at the start of the Premier League campaign. Photograph: Alex Ferrelly/Crystal Pix/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock

This season the defending champions, Arsenal, will have the longest-serving manager in the Premier League. Mikel Arteta has been in charge since 2019 and delivered his first title last season; Aston Villa’s Unai Emery is second on the list, with Leeds’ Daniel Farke third.

The upcoming campaign will set a record for the most new managers at the start of a Premier League season. The nine new names in the dugout are:

Marco Rose – Bournemouth

Xabi Alonso – Chelsea

Pierre Sage – Crystal Palace

Álvaro Arbeloa – Fulham

Gary O’Neil - Ipswich Town

Andoni Iraola – Liverpool

Enzo Maresca- Manchester City

Matthias Jaissle – Newcastle

Oliver Glasner – Nottingham Forest

View image in fullscreen Álvaro Arbeloa will take charge of Fulham after Marco Silva left to join Benfica. Photograph: Javier García/Shutterstock

Biggest signings

There have been hundreds of signings in this summer’s transfer window and many have caught fans’ attention. Here are five to keep an eye on for this upcoming season:

Elliot Anderson: Nottingham Forest to Manchester City For a short time this summer, Anderson’s £116m move to Manchester City was a record transfer for a British player. The signing comes as part of City’s renovated midfield, with Rodri, Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders leaving the club.

Morgan Rogers: Aston Villa to Chelsea The versatile forward was the player to eclipse Anderson’s record. Chelsea paid £117m for the Aston Villa star, who alongside Anderson helped England finish third at the World Cup. The 24-year-old is a huge loss for Villa; Rogers scored 10 goals and made seven assists in the Premier League last season.

Bruno Guimarães: Newcastle to Arsenal This move was an astute one for the Premier League holders. Guimarães is an experienced and reliable midfielder who will add depth to Arsenal’s engine room. Arsenal’s sporting director, Andrea Berta, said: “With Bruno joining us, we are further strengthening the heart of our team. Bruno can play as a defensive midfielder and as a box-to-box player. He combines quality with quantity, and has provided goals and assists for his team every year.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Bruno Guimarães will add experience and adaptability to Arsenal’s midfield. Photograph: Adrian Dennis/AFP/Getty Images

Gonzalo García: Real Madrid to Fulham García became a regular first-team presence for Real Madrid last season, and he has followed his manager for the second half of that campaign, Álvaro Arbeloa, to Fulham. Leaving Madrid for the first time, the highly rated striker needs to adapt quickly to the Premier League.

Thomas Meunier: Lille to Sunderland Sunderland have signed an experienced international in Meunier. The former PSG and Dortmund defender has amassed 83 caps for Belgium and won 14 trophies across his club career.

New kids on the block (or are they?)

The three promoted clubs all have plenty of Premier League history: Hull City, Coventry City and Ipswich Town.

The Tractor Boys won promotion in 2024 but were relegated the following season. Kieran McKenna managed to regain the club’s Premier League status after finishing second in the Championship. He will not be joining them in the top flight, though, as he stepped down to take a break from management. That means Gary O’Neil is back in the Premier League after last taking charge of Wolves.

View image in fullscreen Gary O’Neil is back in the Premier League in charge of newly promoted Ipswich. Photograph: Daniel Weir/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock

Hull were last in the top flight in 2016-17 and their first season there in a decade will be overseen by Sergej Jakirovic, who steered them to an unexpected promotion.

Coventry have spent 25 years out of the top flight and even dropped down to League Two. They have fought their way back up the pyramid with Frank Lampard engineering their Championship-winning campaign. The former Chelsea player and manager will lead the team this season, his first managerial position in the Premier League since his caretaking stint at the Blues in 2023.

Television and radio

Sky Sports and TNT Sports will remain the live TV broadcasters for the Premier League in the UK, with the BBC showing highlights on Match of the Day, but there are some slight changes this season.

The Premier League will allow on-field discussions between players and referees to be aired during live broadcasts. This will be trialled first and will not be present during the opening weekend.

Match of the Day will feature new pundits in the former Brentford and Spurs manager Thomas Frank, plus former players Toby Alderweireld, Robbie Keane and Ashley Young.

The BBC will no longer be airing its fantasy Premier League podcast Fantasy 606. The broadcaster Alistair Bruce-Ball confirmed the news in July, saying: “It’s our amazing listeners’ contributions who really made it. Thank you for listening, for sending your emails, your poems, your songs and for managing the listeners’ teams – we are really going to miss it!”

Sports.title: European playoffs: Rangers scrape first-leg win as Brighton draw in Norway
Sports.content:
Ryan Naderi’s second-half strike gave an unconvincing Rangers a narrow 1-0 win in the first leg of their Conference League playoff tie against Czech side Jablonec at Ibrox. Derek McInnes got his first win as Rangers manager at the fifth time of asking with a 5-1 thumping of St Mirren on Sunday but there was regression in the goalless first half which brought boos at the interval whistle.

The Govan side pepped up after the break and Naderi opened the scoring from close range in the 50th minute but in the 78th minute the substitute Cammy Devlin was sent off – minutes after coming off the bench – for a high tackle on Jiri Slama to leave Rangers to see out the game with 10 men.

Fabian Hürzeler, admitted: “It’s not the result we hoped for,” after Brighton were held to a frustrating goalless draw against Tromsø in Norway. The Seagulls, who open the new domestic campaign against Aston Villa on Sunday, created several good chances but could not find a way past the Tromsø keeper Jakob Haugaard.

View image in fullscreen Brighton players applaud the fans after their draw at Tromsø. Photograph: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images

The winger Ibrahim Osman – making his Brighton debut after three loan spells away – looked particularly lively during the first half. Tromsø then almost snatched a late winner on the break, but the defender Isak Vadebu sent his shot wide as the tie went into next week’s second leg at the Amex Stadium all square.

Hearts’ head coach, Wouter Vrancken, hopes James Wilson’s stunning goal in the 2-2 Conference League draw with Rapid Vienna is a sign of things to come from the youngster. He drilled in an unstoppable drive from 30 yards just moments after coming on as the hosts took the lead in the playoff first leg.

“He’s a young lad so for sure it will be extra special. Let’s hope he can make the next steps,” Vrancken said.

Wilson’s effort marked an impressive turnaround after Josh McPade cancelled out Serge-Philippe Raux-Yao’s first-half header. However, Rapid scrambled in a late equaliser through Nikolaus Wumbrand to ensure the tie remains on a knife edge ahead of next week’s return leg.

David Gray, the Hibernian head coach, savoured “a massive performance and a massive result” as his side kept themselves on course to reach the main phase with a spirited 0-0 draw in Belgium against Gent.

For the second Thursday night in a row, Hibs ground out a stalemate on foreign soil after they eliminated Shkendija in North Macedonia last week. It could have been even better for them if Owen Elding’s 15th-minute penalty had not been saved by Davy Roef.

Motherwell made a whirlwind start at home to Freiburg, with Regan Charles-Cook sidefooting in Emmanuel Longelo’s cutback after just 73 seconds. But Matthias Ginter headed Freiburg level on 27 minutes and netted a second from the spot, after Martin Moormann was shown a straight red card on 65 minutes via a video assistant referee review.

The substitute Keisuke Goto added a third with a stoppage-time header to leave the Scottish side with a 3-1 deficit mountain to climb in Germany next Thursday.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Northern Irish champions, Larne, took a big step towards the league phase after a 2-0 win at 10-man Lincoln Red Imps.

The match looked set to finish goalless in Gibraltar after Red Imps had held firm following Yussef Flalhi’s 29th-minute red card. However, visiting Larne made their pressure pay when Paul O’Neill struck with five minutes left before fellow substitute Kevin O’Hara’s stoppage-time breakaway goal ensured Gary Haveron’s side will have a cushion ahead of the second leg at Inver Park.

Shamrock were held to a 1-1 draw at home by the Finnish side KuPS after they conceded an 85th-minute equaliser. The former Sheffield United full-back Enda Stevens put the Irish side ahead after 49 minutes, but they were denied a precious victory when the one-time Charlton youngster Piotr Parzyszek levelled late on at Tallaght Stadium.

View image in fullscreen Mohamed Salah had a tricky night against Ferencvaros. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

In the Europa League, Mohamed Salah played all 90 minutes of his home debut as Trabzonspor hosted Ferencvaros, but the Hungarian side won 1-0 and their Turkish opponents had Chibuike Nwaiwu sent off in added time.
