Sports.title: Tottenham set to shatter £300m summer transfer spend after agreeing £85m deal with Manchester City for Savinho - and MORE arrivals are expected before window slams shut
Sports.content:
Tottenham have agreed a deal worth £85million for Manchester City winger Savinho. The fee is £75m plus a further £10m in potential add-ons, a record sale for City. Savinho's arrival will push Spurs' spending this summer past £300m, although they have recouped about £140m through the sales of Cristian Romero, Djed Spence and Luka Vuskovic. They plan to spend even further however as talks continue over the purchase of Omar Marmoush from City and Liverpool's Cody Gakpo is among their other targets. Daily Mail Sport first revealed Spurs' bid to sign Savinho on May 25 and the Brazilian agreed to the move early on but City's valuation is understood to have fluctuated owing to the inflated prices in the market. They have also been working to add a replacement with Allan Elias of Palmeiras now in their sights. Tottenham have secured a £75m deal plus £10m add-ons for Manchester City star Savinho Daily Mail Sport first reported Spurs' rekindled interest in the winger in late May of this year

Your browser does not support iframes.

Savinho, 22, will have a medical before signing a long-term contract. The Brazilian's move has been over 12 months in the making, with Spurs first attempting to sign him last summer. After finishing a second-consecutive season 17th in the Premier League, Tottenham have recruited bullishly this summer in a bid to stop the rot. Spurs have spent £185m on bolstering their midfield with the eye-catching signings of Sandro Tonali from Newcastle, and West Ham's Matheus Fernandes, with the club's business not yet finished.

Sports.title: 'Banned because refs can't do their job': Championship star is handed two-match ban for 'successful deception' with handball goal in incredible decision which has left fans of ALL clubs furious
Sports.content:
'Banned because refs can't do their job': Championship star is handed two-match ban for 'successful deception' with handball goal in incredible decision which has left fans of ALL clubs furious

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

West Bromwich Albion star Aune Heggebo has received a two-match ban after scoring a goal with his arm – but the retrospective decision has incensed supporters online.

Heggebo netted the effort during the Baggies' 2-1 win against Norwich at Carrow Road on Saturday, when he bundled in a cross from new signing Jimmy-Jay Morgan after the ball struck his left arm.

Norwich players surrounded referee Tim Robinson – who had missed the incident – to protest the handball, but the goal stood with no further intervention from the officials.

Days later, however, and West Brom were unable to overturn the FA charge that Heggebo had 'successfully deceived a Match Official by handling the ball in a direct successful attempt to score a goal'.

The 25-year-old is now set to serve a two-match suspension for the offence, which is believed to be the first of its kind in English football since a 2024-25 rule change.

But fans on social media suggested that the punishment did not quite fit the 'crime', claiming instead that officials were at greater fault than the Norwegian striker.

Aune Heggebø’s goal for West Bromwich Albion against Norwich City has fuelled controversy over an alleged handball.



Should the goal have stood? 💭 pic.twitter.com/TcKQ4ctV9N — ITV Football (@itvfootball) August 15, 2026

Fans have hit out at the decision to penalise Aune Heggebo for his handball goal on Saturday

'Not sure about that at all,' one fan wrote. 'It’s the officials’ fault for not spotting it.

'The lack of VAR comes with clangers like this, which will always be a major talking point but that’s a very dangerous precedent to be setting.'

Another added: 'This is an absolute disgrace. A ban because the officials can't do their job. Wow.'

A third agreed: '2 game ban because refs are pony. Blows my mind how much protection they get ( feels good being able to say this now ).'

'A player has been banned because the officials failed to spot a handball for a goal,' another supporter commented. 'Joke.'

West Brom had first appealed the charge on Wednesday, with their statement published after the charge was upheld explaining that their claim had been that 'the ball took a deflection from the goalkeeper immediately before making contact with Heggebo’s arm, which materially affected the ball's trajectory and left him with less than 0.1 of a second to react.

'Given the accidental nature of the handball, the club argued it could not be reasonably viewed as a deliberate act of deception,' the statement added.

West Brom also threw their continued support behind their player, going on to add: 'We remain steadfast in our support of Aune, whose character and integrity have been evident throughout his time at The Hawthorns.'

At full-time after the match, Norwich manager Philippe Clement also reserved blame for the officials.

'It was clearly with the arm that the player scores – we could see that from where we were watching, 50 yards away,' Clement said after the game. 'It was the decisive moment in the game and should have been spotted.

'There are four officials and one of them should have seen it. Maybe the referee didn't have the best view – but the linesman on our side needs to see that.

'Missing game-changing moments like this shouldn't happen – it has cost us at least two, maybe three points.'

Sports.title: Arsenal complete Ezri Konsa signing: Premier League champions land Aston Villa star in £55m move hours before beginning title defence
Sports.content:
Arsenal complete Ezri Konsa signing: Premier League champions land Aston Villa star in £55m move hours before beginning title defence

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Arsenal have completed the signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa.

England defender Konsa, 28, has signed a four-year contract with an option for a further year with the Premier League champions.

The 28-year-old had his medical on Thursday ahead of completing his £55m move from Aston Villa - the fee is £51m plus £4m in add-ons.

The Gunners' latest signing arrives hours before they begin their title defence against newly-promoted Coventry City at the Emirates Stadium.

The fee is a triumph for Villa as Arsenal initially valued the 28-year-old, who had two years remaining on his contract, at £30m.

He was not part of Unai Emery's squad for the UEFA Super Cup defeat to Paris Saint-Germain last week as he was away on holiday after the World Cup.

Arsenal have signed Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa in a £51million deal

Konsa featured 48 times last term in all competitions, scoring two goals and contributing one assist, as Unai Emery's side lifted the Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League to secure Champions League football for 2026-27.

He also sported the armband in John McGinn's absence as Villa's vice captain.

Konsa played in every game of England's World Cup run as the country finished third.

Konsa started seven of the Three Lions' eight matches at the tournament, with Thomas Tuchel largely partnering him with Marc Guehi at the heart of the defence.

He also filled in at right back during England's quarter-final victory over Norway.

Sports.title: PREMIER LEAGUE PREDICTIONS: Our experts pick which side will win title, who will go down, biggest flop and best new signing ahead of the new season
Sports.content:
PREMIER LEAGUE PREDICTIONS: Our experts pick which side will win title, who will go down, biggest flop and best new signing ahead of the new season

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It's been a long 12 weeks since the final day of the 2025-26 season but football fans can finally rejoice - the Premier League is back.

With a bang, too. Liverpool, Manchester City, Chelsea, and Newcastle are just a clutch of the boldfaced names with new managers to keep an eye on, and anticipation is rising to see the summer rebuilds clubs have ushered in.

Now, on the eve of the return of top-flight football, Daily Mail Sport experts Oliver Holt, Ian Herbert, Mike Keegan, Kieran Gill, Lewis Steele, Matt Barlow, Bobby Manzi, and Riath Al-Samarrai make their final predictions.

Tip to win the Premier League

Oliver Holt: Arsenal – they have made two good signings over the summer so far and sold prudently. They have strengthened from a position of strength. They look like a side that will be liberated by the confidence of being champions.

Ian Herbert: Arsenal - crossing the Rubicon to claim the title means so much, removes so much pressure. An excellent transfer window has made them stronger

Arsenal have got the devil off their back by wining their first Premier League title under Mikel Arteta and look stronger than ever

Chelsea welcome Xabi Alonso to Stamford Bridge unburdened by European football and having made key summer signings

Mike Keegan: Chelsea. We saw last season what an absence of European football can do at Manchester United and I like what I have seen at Stamford Bridge this summer given their recruitment pivot. The manager is top class and the old heads they have brought in could be enough for a stunning title assault.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Arsenal. They have the best squad, the least turbulence and have dismantled the mental barriers that previously dominated these conversations. The team to beat.

Kieran Gill: Arsenal. They are more settled than everyone else with Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea going through transitions under new managers. I’m not sure it will even be a close title race.

Lewis Steele: Arsenal. Best team by a distance last season. Manchester City were only close because the Gunners kept on stumbling and keeping them alive. Now, Mikel Arteta’s men will not have the tag of ‘bottlers’ or ‘chokers’ and that will free them up. I’d not be surprised if they won by 10 or more points.

Matt Barlow: Arsenal. Long time since they won back-to-back but strong and stable with main rivals in various degrees of flux. Bruno Guimaraes will improve them. Confident in the knowledge they have what it takes. Free from the anxiety of old.

Bobby Manzi: Arsenal appear stronger than last season, so this will no doubt be proved foolish come the end of the season. But Chelsea have an intelligent manager, have added experience to their squad and no European football to contend with - enabling them to focus on domestic glory. Alonso, against all odds, won the league invincible at Bayer Leverkusen. Chelsea look a good outside bet.

Completing the top four

Oliver Holt: Liverpool, Manchester City, Chelsea. For different reasons, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak had disappointing seasons with Liverpool last season. Both can flourish this year and Liverpool have new signings to complement them. Chelsea have a first class manager, no European commitments and a more realistic recruitment policy. City have the muscle-memory of previous greatness.

Ian Herbert: Chelsea, Tottenham, Manchester United. Something about Roberto de Zerbi’s energy allied to the big spending makes me think Spurs will be a big story this season. Chelsea on the up, too, but transition time for Manchester City and Liverpool

Mike Keegan: Arsenal will not be far off. You can’t judge City on a Community Shield but, for me, the jury remains firmly out on Enzo Maresca. Liverpool will improve under Andoni Iraola.

Alexander Isak endured a difficult first season at Liverpool but will be a major weapon fully fit

Riath Al-Samarrai: Liverpool, Manchester City, Chelsea. I don’t envision any of them making a sustained run on Arsenal, but a lot will depend on how quickly Liverpool adapt to Iraola’s style. That’s typically a slow process and a rapid finish. I can see them leading the chase.

Kieran Gill: Chelsea in second, City in third, Liverpool in fourth. Perhaps I’m thinking a tad optimistically on behalf of Xabi Alonso, but he is a good manager who has wielded his influence this summer.

Lewis Steele: Liverpool. People are sleeping on the ability of a much-improved Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz. Their XI is very good but beyond that, it is a worry. Manchester City because they have a deep squad and did not deserve the overreaction or ridicule that came after losing a glorified friendly but losing Pep Guardiola, Bernardo Silva, Rodri and John Stones in the same summer rips their heart out. I’ll go with Chelsea in fourth as I like Xabi Alonso.

Matt Barlow: Chelsea, Liverpool, and Man City. I'm expecting Xabi Alonso to get a tune out of the mass of talent at Chelsea, Liverpool’s big signings from 2025 to improve and City to fade post-Pep Guardiola and post-Rodri but still have lots of quality and Erling Haaland’s goals.

Bobby Manzi: Arsenal, Man United, Man City. Arsenal are nailed on for the top two but will find the first couple of weeks without William Saliba difficult. Manchester United have executed intelligent summer business - they had to improve their midfield and they have. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba are a great blend. As long as Michael Carrick was not a one-hit wonder, they will be up there. A new era at Manchester City but they still have a strong squad to creep into the top four.

The three going down

Oliver Holt: Newcastle almost got sucked into a relegation battle last season. Since then, they’ve lost their biggest asset, Eddie Howe, and their three best players, Anthony Gordon, Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali. Their Saudi owners appear to have disconnected. I like Gary O’Neil, the Ipswich boss, but Ipswich are a classic yo-yo club. And I don’t think Hull have enough to stay up.

Ian Herbert: Fulham, Coventry and Ipswich. Fulham seem a perfect storm: inexperienced new manager, good players have left, an attempt to introduce new system to a club lacking intensity last season. There’s a bond about Hull City. I suspect they’ll be OK.

Newcastle have seen their ranks depleted and a successful manager depart ahead of the start of the season

Mike Keegan: Sunderland, Ipswich Town, Hull City. I’ll probably be the only one predicting Sunderland and I wish I wasn’t because they’re a great club with great fans but they massively overachieved last season and European football this time around could be a killer.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Hull, Ipswich, Fulham. That’s putting a certain amount of faith in Coventry, but Fulham have lost a strong manager and their best player in Harry Wilson. I think they’ll struggle.

Kieran Gill: Ipswich, Hull, Sunderland. I have a hunch that Coventry under Frank Lampard will surprise us, while Sunderland may struggle juggling European football with everything else.

Lewis Steele: Going to be boring and say the three promoted teams. I do think Sunderland will struggle from a bit of second-season syndrome but I think they have just enough quality with Enzo Le Fee, Granit Xhaka, Brian Brobbey et al.

Matt Barlow: Ipswich, Hull, Coventry. Those coming up can all take inspiration from last season’s survivors and there some established teams should be worried by the radical summer of change including Newcastle, Fulham and Palace but the gap still yawns.

Bobby Manzi: Coventry, Hull, Ipswich. Quite simply, the promoted sides are not better than any of the other 17 sides. Coventry have the best chance of staying up but they are lacking in defence.

The biggest overachievers will be

Oliver Holt: Spurs – they have bought well in the summer and in Roberto de Zerbi, they have one of the best managers of this generation. Like Chelsea, they have no European football to drain their resources. They’ll put their recent struggles behind them in style although they could do with a new striker.

Ian Herbert: Everton - drab end to last season obscured the way that David Moyes, such a fine and still underrated manager, has rescued them from annual purgatory. Some good recruits this summer. Moyes buys well. Europe calls.

Mike Keegan: Chelsea, followed by Coventry, who I think will defy the odds and stay up.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Brentford. Again. A smart club with a smart plan and they haven’t been raided quite like Brighton, who would be my second choice if they didn’t have to content with European commitments.

Kieran Gill: I may have hinted at this in my previous answer, but I’ll plump for Coventry. I’m not saying they will suddenly secure Europe. That’s a stretch. Somewhere towards the midtable would be cool.

Lewis Steele: A Brighton or Bournemouth could really flourish but may be held back by Europe. After finishing 17th twice in a row, lowly relegation fodder Spurs might climb up the table…

Tottenham have recruited intensely over the summer, luring Sandro Tonali from Newcastle in a bid to avoid a third 17th-place finish in three seasons

Matt Barlow: Leeds - finished last season at a gallop and reinforced in the summer market. Three winnable home fixtures to start at fortress Elland Road can build a platform for a strong season as others from mid table tackle complications of Europe

Bobby Manzi: Brentford. They were so close to Europe last season - missing out on goal difference. Many tipped them to go down under Keith Andrews and they defied expectation. This season, they may just get Europe. With Bournemouth, Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Brighton all playing on Thursday nights, the teams in the middle of the pack could suffer a drop-off in the league. Brentford have kept the majority of their squad from last season together and added sprinkles of quality such as Mamadou Sangare in midfield. They appear well positioned.

The biggest underachievers will be…

Oliver Holt: Manchester City – I know I’ve got City down to finish in my top four but I don’t think they’ll challenge for the title. It’s always tough when a great manager leaves a club after a long time in charge and I don’t think it will be any different for City. It’s a huge test for Enzo Maresca.

Ian Herbert: Newcastle – car crash summer from a club the Saudis couldn’t be bothered to administer properly, now led by a managerial novice. You’re well out of it, Eddie.

Mike Keegan: Manchester United. There is time left in the transfer window for United to strengthen but, as things stand, I do not think they have made the additions which will deliver another Champions League finish.

Riath Al-Samarrai: A three-way tie between Manchester United (thin squad), Newcastle (decimated squad and technical area) and Aston Villa (great expectations after last season but a pretty horrible summer of departures).

Kieran Gill: Aston Villa. As good of a manager as Unai Emery is, Villa have sold some big names this summer, from Morgan Rogers to Lucas Digne to Youri Tielemens, so I’m concerned they may struggle.

Aston Villa have seen their squad stripped of a number of key talents and have European tests to come later in the season

Lewis Steele: Newcastle. The bubble has burst. I did think it was probably right for Eddie Howe to move on but losing Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon in the same window stinks.

Matt Barlow: Aston Villa. Challenging season ahead for Unai Emery. Lost Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne. Ezri Konsa leaving. Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins unsettled. Key staff gone, too. And has a Champions League campaign to plot.

Bobby Manzi: Bourmemouth. It’s only natural to have a comedown after last season, finishing sixth on 57 points and securing Europa League football for the first time. Much like with Palace last season, playing Thursday-Sunday will take its toll domestically. A bottom-half finish but a strong European return for the Cherries.

Player of the season

Oliver Holt: There are early signs that Arsenal may have cast off the nerves that afflicted them last season. If they play with more freedom and justify their tag as favourites, Bukayo Saka may rediscover his best form.

Ian Herbert: Declan Rice was the orchestrator and architect of so much about Arsenal last season. I can see him running a side that’s feeling mentally released and free.

Mike Keegan: Cole Palmer. A summer off is incredibly rare in this world of saturated football and the mysteriously-omitted England winger will have a barnstormer.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Easy answer would be Haaland, again, but I’ll go with Odegaard at Arsenal. He looks fit and sharp again, which wasn’t always the case last season, but it’ll be interesting to see how Arteta constructs the puzzle with Rice and Guimaraes (who might well be the star turn – the guy can do everything).

Cole Palmer has had a summer off after an injury-stricken season and should be raring to go

Kieran Gill: Joao Pedro. Just because of what I’ve seen of him in Chelsea’s handful of pre-season games. He’s looking like a superstar, and it is understood he is set to sign a new contract.

Lewis Steele: Since I cover Liverpool I will keep my regular readers happy by going with Isak. I’ll look silly when he does his hamstring on Sunday.

Matt Barlow: Alexander Isak. Back to full fitness after his awful first season at Liverpool and sure to enjoy Andoni Iraola’s full throttle style.

Bobby Manzi: Erling Haaland. Goals, goals, goals. At the World Cup, Haaland proved he can find the back of the net regardless of who is around him - scoring seven in five matches. He’s a machine. Nobody will get close to him.

Signing of the summer (so far)

Oliver Holt: Jordan Henderson – not just because he still retains much of the quality he had in his prime but because he is a symbol of a change in approach that Chelsea desperately needed. Xabi Alonso has some brilliant young players at his disposal but it has to be leavened with experience and Henderson and Danny Welbeck are fine professionals who will provide that.

Ian Herbert: Bruno Guimaraes will look even classier in a world class midfield and his presence will free up Rice. Some tandem they’ll be. The £75m salary may come to look excellent value.

Mike Keegan: Youri Tielemans. For the first time in a long time, Manchester United have signed a player who looks like a Manchester United player. I think he’ll settle quickly at Old Trafford and a much-needed all-round presence in midfield.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Harry Wilson to Leeds for nothing.

Kieran Gill: Arsenal’s £75m landing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle. He should fit into that midfield beside Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard nicely.

Bruno Guimaraes represents a coup for Arsenal's recruitment after his move from Newcastle

Lewis Steele: I like some of the low-key ones like Joao Gomes to Aston Villa and Ousmane Diomande to Nottingham Forest and Antonio Silva to Bournemouth. But for the sake of picking one I’ll go Matheus Fernandes.

Matt Barlow: Maxence Lacroix. Should bring much needed leadership and maturity to the heart of Chelsea’s young team and not bad value in today’s world of head-spinning fees.

Bobby Manzi: Youri Tielemans. Manchester United have been gradually improving their squad to mount a title charge by 2028. Last season they bought a new forward line; this season it is the midfield. £35million for one of the best midfielders in the league who is in his peak is the best pound-for-pound signing of a window where midfielders are moving for £100m-plus. Technical Tielemans will give United control of games from deep alongside contributing goals and assists.

The signing I'm not sure about is…

Oliver Holt: It hasn’t happened yet but if it does, I think Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City would be a mistake that would upset the balance and the ethos of the club.

Ian Herbert: Andrey Santos. A curious and very substantial £50m layout on a player who doesn’t really seem to have proved himself as a stellar talent at Chelsea. Odd summer for United.

Mike Keegan: James Trafford. I like Trafford. He’s down-to-earth, a character and clearly a talented shot-stopper. However, in this era of set-piece coaches and goals from corners, I do wonder if he has the physical presence to ensure he lives up to his £40m fee.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Sandro Tonali at Tottenham. The price tag is astronomical.

Kieran Gill: Alejandro Garnacho. Aston Villa have taken a chance on him with a loan – and a conditional obligation to buy – and he has a ton to prove.

Alejandro Garnacho remains a risky deal for Aston Villa after his uneven season in west London

Lewis Steele: Carlos Baleba to Manchester United if it happens. Brighton fans don’t seem bothered about him leaving.

Matt Barlow: Elliot Anderson. Quality player but a huge fee brings great expectation and a difficult time to join Manchester City at the end of an era.

Bobby Manzi: Luka Vuskovic. A teenage defender with a very high ceiling but £50m is a significant outlay for a centre-back who hasn’t played in the Premier League and still has plenty of development ahead of him. He will make mistakes this season - he’s young. Brighton just have to hope he fulfils his potential and eventually reaches his projected future sell-on value. After all, their model is based on calculated risks.

Manager with the most to prove

Oliver Holt: It has to be Enzo Maresca. Following Pep Guardiola is the toughest task in world football and that is Maresca’s fate. Far from universally popular at Leicester City, he left Chelsea in difficult circumstances. I’m not sure he has the personality or the people skills to lead a club of City’s size. If he does, he will join the elite of world coaching.

Ian Herbert: Enzo Maresca. The expectation will be that the prophet of Pep will simply pick up his reins, but history, his own temperament and the Community Shield tell us otherwise. Spectre of those 115 Premier League charges still a shadow on the wall.

Mike Keegan: Xabi Alonso. He got the big gig and, to say it didn’t go well, would appear to be a significant understatement. Arrives at Stamford Bridge with a big point to prove post-Real Madrid, and I think he will do just that.

Enzo Maresca is stepping into enormous shoes at the Etihad as he replaces his former boss Pep Guardiola at Man City

Riath Al-Samarrai: Enzo Maresca at Manchester City, obviously. Seemed a little too pleased with some half-decent work at Chelsea and those shoes he is filling at City are huge.

Kieran Gill: Enzo Maresca. Following Pep Guardiola is no easy task, but Manchester City paid Chelsea a total of £17m to hire him. That brings immediate pressure at a club used to winning.

Lewis Steele: Enzo Maresca. Everyone is out to get him as we saw with the vultures descending on a glorified friendly defeat against the best team in the country. He has a lot of doubters to silence. Same goes for Andoni Iraola, Xabi Alonso, the list goes on…

Matt Barlow: Enzo Maresca. Just the 15 major trophies in 10 years for Pep Guardiola, follow that.

Bobby Manzi: Alvaro Arbeloa. Arbeloa is a bit of an unknown quantity. Interim at Real Madrid for five months at the end of last season, having previously held youth roles, this is his first genuine crack at senior management. His record at Real was okay with a 64.29 per cent win rate, losing eight games. That would be more than acceptable at Fulham, not so much at Real. But he was credited for how he lifted the dressing room after a tough spell under Alonso. Fulham have enjoyed stability in recent years under Marco Silva: Arbeloa must show he can provide that.

Sports.title: Man United boss Michael Carrick says it is 'ridiculous' to suggest they have an easy start against Hull and Ipswich - and plays down talk of a Premier League title challenge
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick says it’s ‘ridiculous’ to suggest Manchester United have been handed an easy start to the season – and admits it’s asking a lot for his team to be considered title challengers.

United kick off the campaign at Hull City on Saturday lunchtime followed by a first home game against another of the newly-promoted teams, Ipswich Town, at Old Trafford the following week.

But Carrick has rejected claims that United have been given an easy ride, saying: ‘There are no favourable starts. It’s an easy thing to throw out there but pretty ridiculous.

‘It’s a tough start against both teams, but we’re not getting past Saturday. A newly-promoted team away from home will be a tough game.

‘That is the beauty of the new season. For teams coming up into the league, there tend to be quite a few changes. That is the challenge playing against them, we are fully aware of that. Mentally and physically we have done a lot of work. We are fully aware of what’s at stake and what’s coming at us.’

On United’s chances of delivering a first Premier League title since 2013 while coping with the demands of a Champions League return, Carrick added: ‘It’s going to be a jump. It doesn’t matter whether I say whether we can or can’t – and I would never say we can’t – it’s about what we can do, and what we are capable of doing as a group.

Carrick has rejected claims that United have been handed an easy start to the season, saying: ‘There are no favourable starts. It’s an easy thing to throw out there but pretty ridiculous'

United hope to add a third midfield signing of the summer after tabling a £65million offer for Brighton’s Carlos Baleba (right)

‘The run of form we had last season gives us confidence, but we know there is a whole new step to make as a group. We have the potential to achieve things and we have to believe we can do good things.’

United hope to add a third midfield signing of the summer after tabling a £65million offer for Brighton’s Carlos Baleba, having already spent £85m on Andrey Santos, of Chelsea, and Aston Villa’s Youri Tielemans. The club are also keen to strengthen at left-back.

Carrick was reluctant to say too much with another 11 days to go until the transfer window closes. ‘I just think we are looking to strengthen the squad, and we are working towards that,’ he said. ‘We’re certainly trying to make the most of the opportunities to finish the window stronger than we went into it, and I think we are in a good way to doing that so far.’

Marcus Rashford’s return from a loan spell at Barcelona has given United another option, and Carrick has been delighted with the England international’s attitude so far.

‘It has been pretty obvious that Marcus came back training with Kobbie (Mainoo) and Licha (Martinez) that he has come back fantastically well,’ added the United boss. ‘He looks strong, sharp and ready to play football. He can play through the middle, even though it’s not his No 1 position. We have forwards that give us that flexibility.’

Carrick had some positive injury news with Mason Mount close to fitness after missing the final two friendlies against Leeds and AC Milan with a foot injury. Benjamin Sesko, Matthijs De Ligt and new No 2 goalkeeper Karl Darlow, none of whom featured in pre-season, are also back in training.

‘Karl has trained this week, he is in good shape,’ said Carrick. ‘Mattha has been out for a long period of time, but he is training, and it’s great to have him back. He won’t be involved but he is in good shape and moving in a good direction, so that is a bonus for us. Ben is back training so that is another positive and we’re looking forward to having him back around the group and getting him some minutes.

‘We’re managing Mason a little bit, but he is very close. He’s touch and go for the weekend really and going into next week. Mason will be back very, very soon, if not immediately, so it's all good.’

Sports.title: Liverpool expected to make improved offer for Brighton for winger Yankuba Minteh after £50m bid was rejected - with club still locked in talks with PSG in deal for Bradley Barcola
Sports.content:
Liverpool expected to make improved offer for Brighton for winger Yankuba Minteh after £50m bid was rejected - with club still locked in talks with PSG in deal for Bradley Barcola

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Liverpool are expected to make an improved offer for Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh after having a £50m bid rejected.

The Gambian is out until October after undergoing surgery on his right leg.

Liverpool reverted to the 22-year-old after considering Ibrahim Mbaye of Paris St Germain too expensive. They are continuing discussions for Bradley Barcola.

Daily Mail Sport reported upon Mohamed Salah’s departure that the Gambia international would feature on a list to bolster the wide forward position this summer.

While talks for Barcola are ongoing, they would preferably like two forwards with Ibrahim Mbaye, also of PSG, one sounded out last week.

Minteh is currently on the sidelines after suffering an injury in Brighton's pre-season win over Roma earlier this month.

Liverpool have approached Brighton over signing winger Yankuba Minteh this summer

Andoni Iraola's side are in the market to sign two forwards, with the club locked in talks over PSG's Bradley Barcola

Minteh has made 73 appearances for Brighton to date since joining from Newcastle in a £30m move in the summer of 2024. He has scored 10 goals and provided nine assists for the Seagulls.

Minteh predominantly plays on the right wing, but has also been used on the left by Fabian Hurzeler.

Meanwhile, Curtis Jones will have a medical at noon on Friday after Liverpool agreed to sell him to Inter Milan for £26.7m plus £4m in bonuses and a 10 percent sell-on.

The six-time England international, who joined Liverpool aged nine, has had his heart set on a move to Serie A for some time after failing to regularly establish himself as a starter at Anfield.

Liverpool are preparing for their first season under new manager Andoni Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot following the Dutchman's dismissal at the end of last season.

After spending over £450million on new signings including Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike last summer, the 2024-25 Premier League champions struggled to reach the same heights again under the Dutchman and only narrowly managed to qualify for the Champions League with a fifth-place finish last term.

Liverpool, who waved farewell to Mohamed Salah, Andrew Robertson and Ibrahima Konate at the start of the summer, have so far recruited centre-half Jeremy Jacquet from Stade Rennais and left winger Victor Munoz from Osasuna ahead of the new campaign.

Sports.title: TNT Sport bosses bemused by Joe Cole after pundit bizarrely claimed Hull City have arrived in the Premier League 'through the back door' and he snubbed call to cover opening game - as Tigers owner hits back
Sports.content:
TNT Sport bosses bemused by Joe Cole after pundit bizarrely claimed Hull City have arrived in the Premier League 'through the back door' and he snubbed call to cover opening game - as Tigers owner hits back

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Joe Cole has sparked a furious response from Hull City fans after claiming the Tigers are already relegated - and saying he put his phone on ‘do not disturb’ to ensure he would not have to be a pundit for TNT Sports at their season opener against Manchester United tomorrow night.

The former Chelsea and England man has triggered outrage in East Yorkshire thanks to comments he made with former West Ham team-mate Carlton Cole on a podcast.

When asked who would be going down this season, Cole said ‘Hull are gone, man’ before claiming that they had arrived in the Premier League ‘through the back door’.

He then added that he had ‘a confession to make’, saying he had been contacted by TNT Sports who ‘tried to slip in Hull on the first day of the season’. ‘I put my phone on Do Not Disturb,’ he said.

Hull City are GOING DOWN! 🗣️🐯



The lads don’t rate Hull’s chances this season 🥺



Watch in full 👉 https://t.co/PuonqV3D90#TheDressingRoom #PremierLeague #PL pic.twitter.com/B1xa8RV4nI — The Dressing Room Podcast (@dressingroomaa) August 19, 2026

Joe Cole has risked the wrath of Hull City fans with comments made on his podcast

Daily Mail Sport understands the comments have left bosses at TNT Sports bemused, with insiders saying Cole was not down to cover the opener at the MKM Stadium, and never had been.

Regardless, it has stoked plenty of emotion in Hull. Sources have disclosed that players and staff are well aware of what was said and intend to use it as motivation for what would appear to be a tough mission ahead.

Fans have taken to social media to highlight what they see as a ‘condescending’ and ‘disrespectful’ attitude, with some even claiming the newly-promoted club, who won the Championship play-off final, should ban Cole from its stadium.

Hull owner Acun Ilicali responded to the comments from both Coles on social media, writing: 'It is disappointing to see my beautiful city criticised by people who should know better.

'As a club we are used to being underestimated and we enjoy it, and we enjoyed it more when were promoted last season.

'The true beauty of a place is in its people, and that’s why, for me, Hull is one of the most beautiful places in the world.

'For me, seeing two ex-players making fun of a deservedly promoted club, is more laughable than the things they were laughing at.'

Sports.title: Coleen Rooney beams with joy as she reveals Man Utd starlet son Kai's GCSE results
Sports.content:
Coleen Rooney beams with joy as she reveals Man Utd starlet son Kai's GCSE results

Coleen Rooney has shared her reaction after her Manchester United prospect son Kai received his GCSE exam results

View 2 Images Coleen Rooney shared her reaction to Kai's GCSE results (Image: Instagram/@coleen_rooney)

Coleen Rooney has announced that her son Kai has passed all of his GCSEs. The 16-year-old Manchester United youngster marked results day alongside his mother, who shared a photo of them grinning together.

‌



Kai, son of club legend Wayne, has been part of United's academy since returning to the club at the age of 11 and recently signed a first-year scholarship deal. The agreement enables Kai to continue his studies while going through United's academy system. He could potentially sign a professional contract once he turns 17.

‌



The teenager's footballing progress was disrupted last season after picking up a season-ending injury in March, sidelining him for the FA Youth Cup final against Manchester City. He had enjoyed a breakthrough campaign before the setback, making his debut for Darren Fletcher's under-18s at the age of 15 and scoring twice while providing an assist across six U18 Premier League outings.

‌



Kai also made his first appearance at Old Trafford last season, featuring for 21 minutes in United's FA Youth Cup fourth-round triumph over Derby County. Having watched her eldest son balance his footballing dreams with his school work, Coleen was delighted to share Kai's exam results on social media.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



In an Instagram post, Coleen wrote: "GCSE results day!! Super proud @kairooney.10... Great results, especially with a busy schedule, all passed and a place in 6th form!! We love you."

It represents yet another landmark moment for Kai, who is striving to strike a balance between his education and desire to emulate his dad. Wayne did not sit his GCSEs at Kai's age, but pursued self-education later in his playing days.

The former England star previously told BBC Sport: "It's no secret that I didn't even take GCSEs but I think people assume because of that that I'm not educated, which is really wrong. I made a conscious effort when I was at Everton and Manchester United to educate myself in a lot of different things, such as black history and religion.

‌



"The reason I did that was because I wanted to hold conversations with my team-mates who are from different backgrounds. That was something I did to help me with my team-mates and help understand how they have been brought up. That's probably something people don't understand about me."

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Meanwhile, Kai returned to the pitch last week after recovering from injury and was part of United's squad for the Otten Cup in Eindhoven. The midfielder confirmed his comeback on Instagram with the caption: "First game back from injury. PSV (A)."

‌



United suffered a 1-0 defeat to hosts PSV in their opening fixture of the tournament, with Kai also part of a 23-man squad that featured Jacey Carrick, son of United boss Michael Carrick. Kai's comeback arrives at a crucial point in his development, as he could become a key player for the U18s this season.

The teenager previously banned his dad from attending games because of the attention Wayne would receive on the sidelines. The 40-year-old was in the stands to watch Kai make his Old Trafford debut last season but later admitted he was underdressed for the occasion.

I thought it was one of them oversized tracksuits what the younger lads are wearing nowadays," he said on The Wayne Rooney Show. "So I tried it on and I thought it was actually quite comfortable, so I kept it on and put a big coat over it and gone to the game.

Sports.title: Amazing Journey to be aimed at £5 million race in Australia after purchase for major stable
Sports.content:
Amazing Journey to be aimed at £5 million race in Australia after purchase for major stable

The improving handicapper has been sold privately by owners Gallagher Bloodstock and will target the Golden Eagle at Randwick, Sydney

View 2 Images Amazing Journey: won the International Handicap under Saffie Osborne (Image: PA)

Progressive handicapper Amazing Journey has been snapped up to compete for Ciaron Maher in Australia, with the nation's second most valuable race, the Golden Eagle, earmarked as his initial objective.

‌



The three-year-old gelding stormed to victory in the £150,000 Moet and Chandon International at Ascot under Saffie Osborne last month for Lambourn trainer Jamie Osborne, but has been sold privately by owners Gallagher Bloodstock.

‌



Jamie Osborne confirmed the horse had departed for Harry Eustace's yard to begin quarantine ahead of his journey to Australia where he will be targeted October 31 contest at Randwick in Sydney, a race offering a winner's purse exceeding £1.25 million.

‌



Osborne told the Press Association: "Will Bourne completed the deal acting for Ciaron Maher and the new connections have the idea of taking him Down Under to aim at the race that Lake Forest won for William Haggas two years ago.

"It is a four-year-olds only seven-furlong race and while Amazing Journey would have a little bit to go to match Lake Forest he is improving fast."

‌



View 2 Images Amazing Journey: to continue career in Australia (Image: PA)

Osborne remained pragmatic about the horse's exit, maintaining there were no conflicting feelings from his stable.

"That is part of the job and it gives us immense satisfaction to be able to buy a thirty grand yearling and sell it on for a significant sum," he said. "When this happens it is very much a success, so I'm pleased for Pat Gallagher who now gets a period of 'free' racing."

Article continues below

Amazing Journey will turn four years old upon arrival, with the Melbourne Spring Carnival at Randwick in Sydney marking the start of their campaign.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 predictions as Arsenal tipped for title and £100m signings flop
Sports.content:
Finally, the wait is over. The 2026/27 Premier League season is finally here.

The new campaign gets underway on Friday evening as defending champions Arsenal take on newly-promoted Coventry City. The two sides have very different ambitions for the upcoming campaign, but for this weekend at least, they are equals.

And that goes for each of the 18 other top-flight clubs, who have made managerial changes, dipped into the transfer market and have gone through gruelling pre-season campaigns.

All of that work will now be given its toughest examination yet as the real stuff gets underway. But what's going to happen throughout the next 10 months?

Mirror Football writers have taken a look into their crystal balls to find out...

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Daniel Orme

Winners: Arsenal

The Gunners are the complete package under Mikel Arteta. They've got a brilliant attack, a formidable midfield and a solid defence. And they've now got the silveware to prove it. With the vast majority of their rivals now in transition, the path is opening up for Arsenal to claim the title yet again.

Top five: Arsenal, Man Utd, Liverpool, Man City, Chelsea

Michael Carrick will be hopeful of carrying on the momentum that United built up last season into the new campaign and seal a Champions League spot. Liverpool and Manchester City also have good enough squads to finish in the top four. Chelsea should also be good enough but a title challenge looks like a pipe dream.

Relegated: Coventry City, Hull City, Fulham

It's easy to tip the promoted clubs to go straight back down and I fear two of them will be slipping back into the Championship in 10 months' time. Hull City have a squad that's simply not good enough for the demands of top-flight football, while Coventry will make more of a fight of it but will still be relegated.

Ipswich's experience of a couple of years ago should see them improve. That could leave a surprise package nervously looking over their shoulders and I think that could be Fulham, who could take some time to adapt to Alvaro Arbeloa's demands so could be playing catch-up.

Surprise package: Leeds United

Daniel Farke's side have upgraded in all of the positions that they needed to this summer - and with some of their established rivals contending with European football, that could see the Yorkshire side take advantage. It would certainly not be a shock to see them secure a spot in the Europa League next season.

Top goalscorer: Erling Haaland

Do I need to explain this one? He's the best striker in the Premier League. He's the best striker in the world. And he will be claiming the golden boot once more.

Image: Getty Images) Getty Images)

Best signing: Youri Tielemans

Given the extortianate market when it comes to central midfielders this summer, Youri Tielemans for just £35m is a bona fide bargain. He adds some serious quality to the heart of the United midfield. And under Carrick, he should be able to elevate his game to even higher levels. It would not be a surprise to see the Belgian seal a number of wins with his penchant for an eye-catching goal.

Biggest flop: Mateus Fernandes

This feels slightly harsh given he's just 21 years of age. But is Mateus Fernandes an £85m midfielder? I'm not totally convinced that he is.

Could he be? Possibly. But as it stands...not quite. That price-tag means that he'll be expected to have an instant impact but I think his contributions will be limited this season which could see the pressure rise.

First manager sacked: Alvaro Arbeloa

Having tipped the Londoners for relegation, I'm also predicting Arbeloa to be cut adrift. He's got no Premier League managerial experience and very little full stop. If and when the chips are down at Craven Cottage, I don't expect Fulham to wait for him to pick them back up.

James Whaling

Winners: Arsenal

With Manchester City in transition and none of the other clubs yet ready to challenge the Gunners, I can see this being something of a procession. After finally ending their long wait for a title, I fully expect Mikel Arteta to go back-to-back and lift the trophy again in May.

The arrival of Bruno Guimaraes makes their already formidable midfield stronger and Christos Tzolis looks an exciting attacking addition.

Top five: Arsenal, Man City, Man Utd, Liverpool, Chelsea

I still expect City to be Arsenal's nearest challengers, mainly due to the firepower of Erling Haaland. Manchester United should carry on their upwards momentum under Michael Carrick and it will be fascinating to see how a reintegrated Marcus Rashford performs. Liverpool should have enough to complete the top four under Andoni Iraola and I fancy Xabi Alonso to return Chelsea to the top table of European football.

Relegated: Coventry, Hull, Crystal Palace

It's always tricky for the promoted sides, unless you're Regis Le Bris' Sunderland, and this year looks like being no different. Hull did incredible to return to the top flight but it's hard to see them beating the drop. Similarly Coventry, back after 25 years and with a feel-good factor under Frank Lampard, but look up against it. Crystal Palace might be a surprise pick, but their manager is a complete unknown and some of their business has been headscratching.

Surprise package: Ipswich

I'm backing the Tractor Boys to break the mould and stay in the Premier League. I think they will benefit from their brief foray in the top division two years ago, albeit under a different manager in Gary O'Neil, who will also reap the benefits of his experiences with Wolves and Bournemouth. Julio Enciso and Abdul Fatawu look like smart additions at the top end of the pitch.

Top goalscorer: Erling Haaland

Do you really want an explanation?

Best signing: Christos Tzolis

OK, so the Belgian Pro League isn't the Premier League. But 43 goals in all competitions from the wing in the last two seasons speak for themselves. Tzolis looks like an upgrade on Leandro Trossard and made a bright start to his Arsenal career in the Community Shield.

Image: Getty Images) Getty Images)

Biggest flop: Elliot Anderson

I want to quantify this, because 'flop' is probably too harsh. I don't think Elliot Anderson is a bad player, or a bad signing. But the transfer fee makes me uncomfortable. He is not a £116million footballer, and that is no slight on his ability. He is also not in the same calibre as Rodri, the player he is tasked with replacing. He's a perfectly good player and well worth his place in the England side. But I cannot seeing him having the impact his price tag should justify.

First manager sacked: Sergej Jakirovic

Hull face Manchester United, Aston Villa and Chelsea in their first four games, travelling to fellow new boys Coventry in the other. A slow start looks very possible and pressure could be on the Tigers boss from early in the campaign.

poll loading Who will win the Premier League title this season? 0+ VOTES SO FAR Arsenal Man City Liverpool Man Utd Any other

Sam Meade

Winners: Arsenal

The Gunners finally got over the line last season and that ended the one nagging doubt you had about them. They've strengthened their squad this summer and their closest challengers are all embarking on new eras, which will make overhauling the champions a tall order.

Top five: Arsenal, Man City, Chelsea, Liverpool, Man Utd

Man City by no means inspired in the Community Shield but have too much to not be up there again whilst Xabi Alonso is perhaps the most impressive of the new managers at top clubs, which could help the Blues make huge leaps. Michael Carrick will see that playing in four competitions makes things a lot harder at Manchester United.

Relegated: Coventry, Ipswich, Hull

This year we could see a return to the unfortunate scenes that has seen all three promoted sides going straight back down. Frank Lampard's Coventry will give survival the best shot, but still fall short.

Surprise package: Newcastle

Despite all the doom and gloom, understandably, I still think they'll be in Europa League contention, which isn't bad for a team who've lost the bulk of their best players, their manager and finished in the bottom half last season.

Top goalscorer: Erling Haaland

Not much to say here, he's utterly elite. A fourth Golden Boot in five seasons would have him among the Premier League's greatest strikers, not that he isn't already.

Best signing: James Trafford

Had some standout moments for Man City as they won the Carabao Cup last year and, now in a Leeds team that will look to further consolidate themselves in the top flight, the goalkeeper will really start making his case to be the Three Lions No 1 in the not too distant future.

Biggest flop: Alejandro Garnacho

His last two years have almost been write offs in Manchester and then Chelsea, Aston Villa now think they can get a tune out of him but Garnacho hasn't look like fulfilling his potential for years. The Argentine has moved on loan, which could become permanent, but this is a risky move, and one that won't pay off.

Image: Getty Images) Getty Images)

First manager sacked: Sergej Jakirovic

The Hull owner is an ambitious man and after gaining promotion despite finishing in sixth, he'll know his window for making the Tigers a Premier League team could be a small one. If he can tempt a good manager to Yorkshire, he will do so as early as possible.

Felix Keith

Winners: Arsenal

What don’t they say about north London buses? You wait 22 years and then two come along at once.

Even before signing Ezri Konsa and the world-class forward we’ve been promised all summer, Arsenal have the best squad and their closest rivals are undergoing rebuilds. It’s a recipe for success.

Top five: Arsenal, Man Utd, Man City, Liverpool, Brighton

Enzo Maresca and Andoni Iraola are going to encounter all sorts of problems as they rebuild this season, leaving the door open for Manchester United to pip them to the best of the rest. There’s something to be said for stability and in Michael Carrick they have that. The failure to shift Marcus Rashford could end up being a blessing in disguise.

Like most summers, Chelsea appear to be a mess, with Xabi Alonso wading through unwanted players every time he arrives at Cobham. Tottenham will improve after splashing the cash but not enough to make it into the top five, leaving Brighton to build on their momentum.

Relegated: Fulham, Hull, Ipswich

Ipswich have spent over £100million on players this summer, but the departure of Kieran McKenna after promotion is a blow they won’t bounce back from. Hull look well short of Premier League quality. And I really fear for Fulham in the post-Marco Silva era. The Portuguese manager made mid-table mediocrity look easy, but Alvaro Arbeloa won’t, sending them down just above a succession of disappointments, in the form of Nottingham Forest, Newcastle and Everton.

Surprise package: Brighton

The Seagulls have finished eighth in the last two campaigns and I fancy them to improve upon it this time around. Much like Bournemouth, their recruitment tends to be spot-on and I could see them building up a head of steam in Spring 2027, despite losing top scorer Danny Welbeck.

Top goalscorer: Erling Haaland

It’s obvious for a reason. He’s won the Golden Boot in three of the last four Premier League seasons and the fact Brentford’s Igor Thiago was the closest to him last time around says a lot.

Best signing: Jeremy Jacquet

Losing a player for nothing is never ideal, but swapping Ibrahima Konate for Jacquet could prove to be a timely upgrade. The Liverpool centre-back pairing of Konate and Virgil van Dijk was ropey last season and Jacquet brings class and composure at such a young age to Liverpool’s backline.

Image: Getty Images) Getty Images)

Biggest flop: Sandro Tonali

I am simply not having £100m for Tonali, who Newcastle fans will tell you was really not that good last season. The Italian is a good midfielder, nothing much more, and Tottenham have grossly overpaid for his services.

First manager sacked: Oliver Glasner

Quiz question: can you name the four managers Nottingham Forest cycled through last season? No cheating. Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis is not a patient man and I’m not sure Glasner is convinced he’s made the right choice after leaving Crystal Palace. If things go south early in the season, the Austrian could be toast.

Andy Dunn

Winners: Arsenal

And while you’re at it, give them the 27-28 title as well. It has been clear for some time that this is an Arsenal squad - and manager - capable of establishing an era of domestic dominance.

A great goalkeeper, a formidable defence and a powerhouse midfield give Mikel Arteta the basis for a team that should rarely be beaten. Add a bit more high-end creativity and firepower, and they could even be invincible.

Top five: Arsenal, Manchester United, Liverpool, Chelsea, Manchester City

United’s transfer business has not been overly dramatic but has been shrewd enough to add to the momentum built by Michael Carrick last season. Andoni Iraola will take a while to become accustomed to the demands of Anfield but will get motoring after a couple of months and Xabi Alonso will restore some sensible football to Stamford Bridge. The post-Pep void will be more painful than City fans imagine and they will only just scrape into the top five.

Relegated: Coventry City, Hull City, Ipswich Town

Deeply unimaginative, for sure, and let’s hope it’s not the case. But it is hard to make a really compelling argument for any of the promoted teams avoiding a relegation battle. One or two of them might battle their way to a points tally that keeps them up but it’s hard to be confident about that scenario. If you are looking for outsiders to get sucked in, Everton and Nottingham Forest might be on your list.

Surprise package: Leeds United

He has been in the firing line a few times but Daniel Farke makes a nice contribution to the Premier League product and his team will continue to entertain. And with James Trafford on board, they have a reliable last line of defence. They will defy their odds.

Top goalscorer: Erling Haaland

Even though it will be a season of struggle for Manchester City, Haaland will do what he always does and dominate their scoring charts. It would not be surprising if Alexander Isak gives Haaland a run for his money and if you are looking for a long shot, look no further than Manchester United’s Benjamin Sesko.

Best signing: Morgan Rogers

At £117million, the England man is not the best-value signing but he will flourish under Xabi Alonso at Chelsea and flourish alongside Cole Palmer.

James Trafford is a corker of a capture for Leeds United.

Image: Getty Images) Getty Images)

Biggest flop: Sandro Tonali

For this era of over-priced midfielders, the Italian is probably the poster player. At £116million, Elliot Anderson will come under scrutiny at Manchester City but Tonali’s price tag - £92.5million rising to £100million - is preposterous. He is not going to single-handedly transform Tottenham Hotspur’s fortunes, that is for sure.

First manager sacked: Sergej Jakirovic

Again, hardly left-field, but the Hull City manager faces a formidable challenge to put points on the board and will be vulnerable early in the season.

Alex Richards

Winners: Arsenal

Hard to back against Mikel Arteta's men. They've consistently improved in the last two years, won the title last term to finally get that monkey off their back and were penalty kicks away from being European champions. Could they be more expansive and exciting? Of course. But they overpower opponents, grind teams down and look like making fewer mistakes than any of their rivals.

Top five: Manchester City, Manchester United, Liverpool, Chelsea

If it looks like the obvious answers, it's because they are. Aston Villa have lost too many key players, Chelsea don't have Europe to contend with and have a new workaholic manager with a point to prove, while City, United and Liverpool all look shoo-ins. Tottenham will improve but probably have too much room to make up.

Relegated: Hull City, Coventry City, Fulham

Of the three promoted teams, I think Ipswich, can keep their heads above water. They've really strengthened and while Kieran McKenna may have gone, Gary O'Neil comes in looking to show that the manager we saw in his final half season at Wolves - ironically sacked after losing at home to the Tractor Boys - isn't really who he is. In his first season at Wolves, and his year at Bournemouth, he did very well to ensure both survived, and can do so again at Portman Road.

If they're staying up, then someone from last season's top-flight mix has to go down, and Fulham are the team who I'm very uncertain about. Along with the exit of Marco Silva, some key, experienced performers have been allowed to depart for pretty minimal sums and they've spent very heavily on the young Real Madrid pair Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios, both known to new boss Alvaro Arbeloa. They don't have an easy start to the season and I think they could be running into a big problem.

Image: Getty Images) Getty Images)

Surprise package: Everton

After finishing 13th last season, I think David Moyes will have them in contention for European places this term. Hayden Hackney is a talented player who should dovetail nicely with Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, Tyrique George is talented and will want to show Chelsea they were wrong. Moyes teams tend to trend upwards in their second full seasons and if they can find a regular goalscorer, be it one currently in situ or a new arrival, then they'll be much improved.

Top goalscorer: Erling Haaland

Next.

Best signing: Andy Robertson

It's been a while since Spurs had anything like a settled defence and they've had issues at left-back for quite some time. Robertson may be 32, but for what Roberto De Zerbi is going to want, he's absolutely ideal, especially considering his arrival as a free transfer. His determination and leadership qualities should also help drag up standards that have too often in the last few years been allowed to slip.

Of all the others, Joao Gomes should help Aston Villa fill a big hole in their midfield while Ousmane Diomande will shine in Oliver Glasner's back three at Nottingham Forest.

Biggest flop: Gonzalo Garcia

Fulham need him to be red hot from the off and throughout the season after paying £34m up front for the young Spaniard, but I'm just not sure he's going to be able to give them what they need as he adapts to not only a new country, but what is effectively his first full season as a bona-fide starter in senior football.

First manager sacked: Sergej Jakirovic

He may have got Hull City promoted, but that won't count for much if they're struggling come the international break.

Sports.title: 11 pundits predict who will win Premier League title with BBC stars in major disagreement
Sports.content:
11 pundits predict who will win Premier League title with BBC stars in major disagreement

With the start of the new Premier League season almost upon us, we're looking at who the nation's top pundits are tipping to lift the trophy in nine month's time

View 5 Images Arsenal are the reigning Premier League champions (Image: Getty)

The waiting is finally over. As the Premier League returns tomorrow, the footballing world beckons forth another nine-month rollercoaster of drama and unrelenting tension.

‌



Before a single ball is kicked on opening weekend, the traditional ritual of pre-season predictions has reached fever pitch, with top pundits across the UK weighing in on who will lift the trophy come May.

‌



After weeks of blockbuster transfers and managerial shuffles, opinion among the game's elite analysts remains fiercely split. Will defending champions Arsenal build on their success and forge a new dynasty, or can a refreshed Manchester City reclaim their crown?

‌



Meanwhile, heavyweights like Liverpool, Manchester United and an ambitious, revamped Chelsea are waiting in the wings, eager to crash the party and disrupt the title narrative. Mirror Football looks at who 11 of the UK's leading pundits think will end the 2026/27 season as champions.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

BBC reveals new Match of the Day line-up with six stars missing and four replacements named READ MORE :

Wayne Rooney - Arsenal

Manchester United legend and BBC pundit Rooney reckons Arsenal will be even better than they were in their title-winning campaign after bringing in Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa. He said on Stick to United: "You’re looking at Arsenal and Man City [for the title].

‌



View 5 Images BBC star Rooney has a clear verdict (Image: Stick to United)

"Chelsea will be a lot better this season, Tottenham will be better. You've got Liverpool in there as well. So it’s going to be tough. Arsenal have the potential to run away with it but behind them we could see a lot of changes.

"I think Arsenal are the favourites to win it but can United nick second off Man City and start to build again and maybe challenge for the title next season?"

‌



Joe Hart - Man City

Hart, ex-City goalkeeper and Rooney's BBC colleague, disagrees and thinks his former side have the edge. He said: "It's really important how Arsenal handle the scrutiny of being champions, but they will totally understand that and what is coming their way.

"City were clunky against Arsenal in Cardiff but I don't think they will overreact to one poor game. I think they still believe they've got the team and the quality to challenge," he added, predicting City to finish first and Arsenal to end up second.

Gabby Agbonlahor - Arsenal

"I'm going with Arsenal," the former Aston Villa forward said on talkSPORT. "They've got the strongest squad, they've been there and done it. We can't judge the teams chasing them yet as they've got new managers – Enzo Maresca in at Manchester City, Andoni Iraola at Liverpool, Xabi Alonso at Chelsea."

‌



View 5 Images Agbonlahor is backing Arsenal (Image: talkSPORT)

Danny Murphy - Arsenal

"Without all the new signings being done yet, it's hard to call, but I think Arsenal will win it again," the BBC's Murphy said. "Mikel Arteta's side will have greater strength in depth than last season and more quality. They also have the confidence and belief from winning it last year.

"They have not lost any of their best players and they have got a group who know what the manager expects from them and are completely on board with it. Arteta didn't need to spend half the pre-season drilling them with his methods like a new manager has to."

‌



Jeff Stelling - Arsenal

"I've done my finishing order for the Premier League, so here we go: Arsenal to win it," Stelling began on talkSPORT. "Chelsea second, Man City third, Man United fourth, Spurs fifth, Liverpool sixth... that's my prediction but I'll probably be miles off it."

Jamie Carragher - Man City

At the start of August, Liverpool legend Jamie Carragher tipped Manchester City to win the Premier League title. However, he warned his view would change if they sold Rodri - and that is exactly what has now happened with the Spaniard joining Barcelona.

"I think City," Carragher said on Football Ramble. "The reason I think City is, they were close last year. I know Pep's gone. I get that. But when you've had the same manager for 10 years, the flip side of what people will say - that's it hard to [follow in his footsteps] - but [Maresca] will offer something a little bit new, a little bit fresh.

‌



View 5 Images Carragher is on City's side (Image: Football Ramble)

"I think if Rodri left for Real Madrid I wouldn't be saying that. But I think where they are right now, I'd go with City... I just think City with a new manager will be so invested in the Premier League.

"With Arsenal I do feel like they will be [focused on] the Champions League. Winning the Champions League for Arsenal is far bigger... if you got to March, April and you were still in the Champions League, that's where you'd go, 'Declan Rice, you're not playing Saturday, you're playing Tuesday in the Champions league.' I'm not sure City will have that."

‌



Shay Given - Man City

"I don't think Pep leaving City means we will see what happened when Sir Alex Ferguson left United. Instead, I am expecting the opposite, because of a fresh voice in the dressing room," the former City goalkeeper predicted. "These players have not won the Premier League in two years so they will be hungry for success. City will be number one."

Leon Osman - Arsenal

"Arsenal look like a team that are ready to have a run at winning three titles in the next four or five years," the ex-Everton midfielder said. "Teams like United in the early Premier League days, Arsenal under Arsene Wenger and Jose Mourinho's Chelsea give me the vibes this team does."

View 5 Images Most pundits think the Gunners will go back-to-back (Image: Getty)

‌



Matthew Upson - Arsenal

"Arsenal are my favourites again but I don't see them running away with it," Upson said. "Staying at the top is always harder - ask any manager - and you also have to remember there were spells when they looked like they had run out of steam last season and were grinding out results a lot of the time."

They are in for Lille's Ayyoub Bouaddi, who is a talented player but he is 18, and would be a massive gamble."

Sports.title: Arsenal 'exploring Kenan Yildiz transfer' with chance of completing blockbuster swap
Sports.content:
Arsenal 'exploring Kenan Yildiz transfer' with chance of completing blockbuster swap

Arsenal still want to sign a forward after missing out on Real Madrid's Vinicius Junior and new Chelsea signing Morgan Rogers, with Mikel Arteta especially keen on Kenan Yildiz

View 2 Images Kenan Yildiz is valued at £60million by Juventus (Image: Filippo Alfero - Juventus FC/Juventus FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal are exploring a move for Juventus star Kenan Yildiz in a deal which could see Gabriel Martinelli go the other way. Yildiz, 21, is high on the Gunners' shortlist and Mikel Arteta in particular wants the German-born Turkey international.

‌



Having agreed a £51million deal to sign Ezri Konsa and in turn alleviate their defensive concerns, Arsenal's focus has switched to signing a forward, particularly one who can play on the left wing. The Gunners were interested in Morgan Rogers before his £117million move to Chelsea and missed out on Vinicius Junior after he decided to extend his contract with Real Madrid.

‌



Now, according to the Independent, Yildiz is being targeted. Juventus would demand north of £60m, a fee which would take Arsenal's net spend this summer to almost £200m after paying sums for Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimaraes and soon enough Konsa.

‌



So, a solution to help balance the books has been discussed. It's reported that although negotiations would be required, Martinelli could be used in a swap deal, with the 25-year-old having been left out of Arteta's squad for the Community Shield.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Yildiz signed for Juventus on a free transfer in the summer of 2022 after coming through Bayern Munich's academy. The 21-year-old enjoyed by far his most productive campaign last season, scoring 11 goals and providing nine assists in 47 appearances, although Juventus could only manage a sixth-place finish in Serie A.

Meanwhile, some thought at Arsenal has been given to waiting until future windows to sign Junior Kroupi from Bournemouth, who was a target prior to his pre-season injury. Julian Alvarez also remains on Arsenal's shortlist and there's a possibility that Atletico Madrid's refusal to sell him to Barcelona, coupled with his desire to leave, could yet present an opportunity for the Gunners.

Arteta has made it clear both privately and in public that Arsenal can't stand still after winning the Premier League title, with their next aim being to lift the Champions League and get their hands on domestic trophies. "Well, we are really active in the market. I think I mentioned that a few days ago," he said on Thursday when asked about their pursuit of Konsa.

‌



"The ambition is to improve the squad. We have a really specific issue in the backline, especially with the long-term injury of Wilo [Saliba] and the fact that we miss one more defender; that's clear. So we are trying to reinforce that area. Whenever we're ready, we'll announce something."

Should Arsenal swap Gabriel Martinelli for Kenan Yildiz? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli's future at Arsenal remains uncertain (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

‌



Arteta went on to admit that some long-serving players such as Martinelli may have to be moved on in order to accommodate new signings. "It's a really, really tough moment, you need to face that reality," he confessed.

"But you need to face it with real honesty and transparency because when you are on the other side, that's exactly what you need. You might not like what you've been told, but if it's truthful, if it's the reality, if it's honest and it's going to help you to make better decisions and have more clarity for the next steps in your career, you have to do that.

"These are always very difficult conversations, but they need to be done. It's like when a player doesn't feel that he belongs or he's important, he wants to have a different chapter, I think that communication has to exist and it has to be both ways.

Article continues below

"We all know, everything has a start and has an end. When it comes to the end, I think our duty, our responsibility is to do it in the best possible way, maintaining the respect and admiration for the player and the relationship, but understanding that at the end, we need to make football decisions."
